4e31e62067f289d2.title: Uttar Pradesh MSME Promotion Policy, 2022: Incentives, eligibility and implementation
4e31e62067f289d2.summary: UP MSME Promotion Policy 2022: Investment support with finance, employment, industrial land, technology, quality and environmental compliance. The policy is one of Uttar Pradesh's principal frameworks for encouraging smaller manufacturing enterprises. Its incentives are deliberately differentiated by both enterprise size and location, with higher support for micro enterprises and for investments in Purvanchal and Bundelkhand . The policy was introduced to improve investment, technology adoption, access to finance, environmental performance and competitiveness among micro, small and medium enterprises in Uttar Pradesh . It applies primarily to manufacturing-oriented MSMEs and supporting industrial infrastructure. Its assistance covers areas such as: The policy should not be confused with schemes such as the Chief Minister's Youth Self Employment Scheme or the Mukhyamantri Yuva Udyami Vikas Abhiyan. Those schemes may provide loans or entrepreneurship support but operate under separate eligibility and financing rules. The notified English version states that the policy was issued through a government order dated September 28, 2022 by the Department of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise and Exports Promotion. The state government described MSMEs as important to Uttar Pradesh's economic growth, employment generation and its broader ambition to expand the state economy. The policy was framed in the aftermath of the Covid-19 pandemic, when smaller enterprises faced disruptions in demand, finance and supply chains. The state also wanted to position Uttar Pradesh as a more competitive destination for new industrial investment as businesses reconsidered manufacturing locations and supply chains. These are policy objectives rather than verified outcomes attributable solely to the scheme. The policy uses the applicable Government of India definition of micro, small and medium enterprises. 7622cfa8239b56d7.title: Last-minute train ticket cancellation costs Railways ₹25,000
7622cfa8239b56d7.summary: Published - November 27, 2026 07:00 am IST - MALAPPURAM A train ticket that was cancelled without warning just before departure has cost the Railways ₹25,000 in compensation and legal expenses. The Malappuram District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission issued the order on a complaint filed by a law student from Manjeri. C. Yadukrishnan, a student of KC Law College in Mumbai, had booked a ticket on Netravati Express through the IRCTC app to travel to Keralam on September 9, 2024. His ticket had been upgraded to RAC 44 but slipped to waiting list one shortly before the journey and was subsequently cancelled. Mr. Yadukrishnan said he had neither cancelled the ticket nor received any advance notification about the change in its status. With the journey at stake, he booked a fresh ticket on the same train to reach Keralam. The original ticket cost ₹1,819, including GST. However, after deducting ₹65 as clerkage charges, the Railways refunded only ₹1,730. In its defence, the Railways said the change in reservation status followed the replacement of a third AC coach with a third AC economy coach due to operational requirements. This had led to the rearrangement of passenger reservations, according to the Railways. The Commission, however, found that the cancellation resulted from a lapse on the part of the Railways. It directed the additional general manager of Central Railway, Mumbai, to pay Mr. Yadukrishnan ₹20,000 as compensation and ₹5,000 towards litigation expenses within 45 days. 4944dfff254a5b04.title: In Rajasthan, the girls who refuse to be spoken for
4944dfff254a5b04.summary: Rajasthan ranks sixth among India’s States with the highest prevalence of child marriage, according to the latest National Family Health Survey (2023-24). Poverty, the lack of education, and entrenched customs such as atta-satta, reinforced by a skewed sex ratio, continue to fuel the practice, particularly in tribal and rural areas. Now, a growing number of girls, empowered by education and greater access to social media, are saying no, reports Ashok Kumar. Meanwhile, the United Nations has declared November 27 as the International Day for the Elimination of Child, Early and Forced Marriage

e354bc12ef9726dc.title: SC suggests Parliament to bring amendment to section 26E of SARFAESI Act
e354bc12ef9726dc.summary: The Supreme Court on Thursday said Parliament should consider bringing an appropriate amendment to section 26E of the SARFAESI Act and that an explanation of the expression "all other debts" in the provision may be provided authoritatively. Section 26E of the SARFAESI Act, 2002, gives secured creditors priority to recover their debts ahead of other debts and government dues once a security interest is registered. A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and Ujjal Bhuyan made the suggestion while referring a legal question -- whether the "deposits" sought to be recovered under the Maharashtra Protection of Interest of Depositors (in Financial Establishments) Act would fall within the ambit of the expression "all other debts" appearing in section 26E of the SARFAESI Act -- to a three-judge bench. a94733a0b04481b7.title: Cultural values of language remain irreplaceable in AI era: Arabic meet
a94733a0b04481b7.summary: Published - November 27, 2026 02:24 am IST - MALAPPURAM E.T. Mohammed Basheer, MP, inaugurating the valedictory session of an international conference on Arabic language at Anvarul Islam Arabic College, Kuniyil, near Areekode, on Thursday. | Photo Credit: SAKEER HUSSAIN Artificial Intelligence (AI) may transform the way Arabic is learned and used, but human emotions and traditional values remain beyond the reach of technology, an international conference on the Arabic language held at Anvarul Islam Arabic College, Kuniyil, observed on Thursday. The two-day conference, titled ‘Digital humanities: reimagining Arabic language and literature’, was organised by the Arabic department of the college in association with Calicut University’s Arabic department, Kerala State Higher Education Council, and Arab Union of Internet Writers. Liyaqat Ali, deputy director of collegiate education, inaugurated the conference on Wednesday. College Principal K. Mohammed Fawaz presided over the function. Liyaqat Ali, deputy director of collegiate education, inaugurating an international conference on Arabic at Anvarul Islam Arabic College, Kuniyil, on Wednesday. | Photo Credit: SAKEER HUSSAIN Arabic scholars Sumayya Ibrahim Abu Thailath from Palestine, Najeeb Ali Mulkhath from Yemen, Simi K. Salim, K. Ali Noufal, I.P. Abdul Salam, C.M. Sabir Navas, K.A. Nasser, P. Firoz, M.K. Ameer Swalahi, Shakir Babu Kuniyil, and K.P. Abdul Haleem Thangal spoke. E.T. Mohammed Basheer, MP, inaugurated the valedictory function on Thursday. He highlighted the growing global significance of the Arabic language in an increasingly interconnected world. Scholars Mujeeb Nellikkuth, Ali Jafar, Mohammed Aman K., P. Sulaiman and C. Abdul Wahab spoke. This would include the methodology and safeguards for recording and verifying caste-related information. A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana took note of the submission made by Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, that she would apprise the court of the relevant SOPs. The bench asked the law officer to provide the details within a week. In its order dated October 12, the bench had requested the solicitor general to place on record the census SOPs being followed. It also directed that a complete set of the paper book be provided to the advocate-on-record for the Centre and the office of the solicitor general. A plea by Aakash Goel raised concerns over the methodology and safeguards for collecting and verifying

bb7356fcd2145168.title: HC to hear Tata Trusts' plea against Chandra's reappointment on Friday
bb7356fcd2145168.summary: The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and the R.D. Tata Trust (RDTT) on Thursday filed suits in the Bombay High Court against Tata Sons and six of its directors, challenging the reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as executive chairman for a third five-year term. The court will hear the matter on Friday. The SDTT has sought Rs 50 crore, while the RDTT has sought Rs 15 crore in damages, with 18 per cent annual interest. As per the suits, the September 17 Tata Sons board resolution to reappoint Chandrasekaran was invalid because it did not receive the affirmative vote required under Article 121 of the company's Articles of Association (AoA). Senior counsel Janak Dwarkadas, appearing for the two trusts, mentioned the suits on Thursday before a single bench of Justice Arif Doctor, seeking an urgent hearing. Justice Doctor, however, recused himself without assigning any reasons, following which the suits were mentioned before Justice Abhay Ahuja, who was sitting on the alternate bench. Dwar

77ea2a96d09fd479.title: Tamil Nadu CM announces 15 days paternity leave for male govt employees
77ea2a96d09fd479.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay on Thursday announced 15 days paternity leave for male government employees, and this is the first time the state has granted men such an entitlement for better parenting. Caring for a child is essential for men as well, and accordingly, married men may avail 15 days paternity leave, the government said. The chief minister has ordered the implementation of a new leave facility for men and the 15 days leave may be availed either 15 days before child birth or within six months following the birth of the baby, an official release said. The government said the move follows representations from employees seeking paternity leave for men and it was positively considered. Women government employees are granted 365 days maternity leave.

409c263256ae8b9f.title: Govt clears six brownfield urea projects worth ₹54,000 crore to boost domestic production
409c263256ae8b9f.summary: New Delhi: The Centre has approved six brownfield urea manufacturing projects involving an estimated investment of ₹ 54,000 crore under the National Investment Policy for Urea (NIPU)-2026 as it looks to expand domestic production capacity, reduce import dependence and strengthen fertiliser security. The projects, spread across Tamil Nadu, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal and Rajasthan, will add a combined annual production capacity of 7.62 million tonnes, with each plant designed to produce 1.27 million tonnes annually. The proposed investments involve public sector undertakings, cooperative institutions and private companies. The six projects include Madras Fertilizers Ltd's (MFL) unit in Chennai, National Fertilizers Ltd's (NFL) Nangal plant in Punjab, KRIBHCO's Shahjahanpur project in Uttar Pradesh, Matix Fertilizers' Panagarh unit in West Bengal, Chambal Fertilizers ' Gadepan complex in Rajasthan and Indian Potash Ltd's (IIPL) proposed unit at Jagdishpur in Uttar Pradesh. With each brownfield project estimated at a capital cost norm of around ₹ 9,000 crore, the 6 urea plants are poised to attract nearly ₹ 54,000 crore in fresh investment, advancing India toward self-reliance (Atmanirbharta) in urea production while generating employment. To strengthen investor confidence and project bankability, the NIPU-2026 framework pairs a balanced 12–16% Return on Equity (RoE) band—anchored by a 12% floor and a 16% ceiling—with a foreign exchange rate mitigation mechanism that normalizes exchange rates and converts into INR after four years based on prevailing rates. Coupled with brownfield advantages that deliver an estimated ₹ 225 crore in annual savings—or roughly ₹ 1,800 crore over eight years—these provisions enhance financial viability and drive sustained capital inflows into domestic fertilizer manufacturing. 0d6de81005df47fc.title: Governor seeks CM’s report on compliance with SC’s directions
0d6de81005df47fc.summary: Published - November 26, 2026 02:46 am IST Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar on Wednesday sought a comprehensive report from Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay on whether the State government had complied with the Supreme Court’s November 20 order on the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam. The move comes in the wake of the ceremonial lamp being lit only at the traditional spot — the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchchipilliyar Temple — on Tuesday, defying the Supreme Court’s direction to light it on the deepathoon atop the Thirupparankundram hillock as a “limited one-time arrangement”. Sources told The Hindu that the Governor had sought a report from the Chief Minister under Article 167(b) of the Constitution, detailing the action taken by the authorities on the Supreme Court’s directions. It came on the heels of the Madurai Collector telling the Supreme Court, in a preliminary status report filed on Wednesday, that he had made every arrangement to comply with the court’s November 20 order to light the lamp on the deepathoon , but the Board of Trustees of the Arulmigu Subramaniyaswamy Temple had failed to authorise a lamp-lighting team. 84529d539f281aa1.title: Rajbanshi language to be included in Eighth Schedule of Constitution: Suvendu Adhikari
84529d539f281aa1.summary: Published - November 26, 2026 03:20 am IST - Kolkata West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. File | Photo Credit: ANI West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) said that the Rajbanshi language will be included in the Eight Schedule of the Constitution, a promise that their party had made during their Assembly election campaign. During the inauguration of a festival in West Bengal’s Cooch Behar district, Mr Adhikari said that their government is taking complete care of the Rajbanshi community, including their language, culture, political aspirations, and financial security. He added that as promised in BJP’s West Bengal Assembly poll manifesto and reiterated by several top BJP leaders during the buildup to the elections, Rajbanshi language is set to be part of the Eight Schedule of the Constitution. “We raised the issue during a meeting with the Union home minister and the home secretary on November 19 that was attended by me and the state’s chief secretary,” Mr Adhikari told reporters before the inauguration of Ras Utsav (annual celebration of Radha-Krishna) festivities in Cooch Behar. At Cooch Behar, Mr Adhikari was greeted by Cabinet minister Nisith Pramanik, a member of the Rajbanshi community. Later, the CM also took part in the festivities in the local area. Mr Adhikari also added that the Rajbanshi community expressed their dissatisfaction over losing their land ownership in the region as he held the Left Front government responsible for it. He also added that the previous governments in the State did not offer much participation of the Rajbanshi community in the cabinet and that their government has done more for the community since they came to power. The Rajbanshi community has always stood by us since 2019, Mr Adhikari added. In the recently concluded assembly polls, the BJP performed exceptionally well in north Bengal and won eight out of nine seats in the Cooch Behar district. Published - November 26, 2026 03:20 am

142fbb823dddf4c5.title: Kallakurichi TVK MLA Arul Vignesh summoned for questioning in harassment case
142fbb823dddf4c5.summary: Updated - November 26, 2026 01:42 am IST - KALLAKURICHI Kallakurichi MLA C. Arul Vignesh’s residence. | Photo Credit: S.S. Kumar The Kallakurichi All Women Police on Wednesday (November 25, 2026) served summons on Kallakurichi TVK MLA C. Arul Vignesh directing him to appear for questioning in connection with a harassment case registered against him on a complaint lodged by a woman IAS officer. Inspector Bhuvaneshwari attached to the All Women Police station visited the MLA’s house in Kallakurichi and handed the summons to him in person. The police also questioned Arul Vignesh at the house. The woman IAS officer had submitted a formal complaint to the Kallakurichi district Superintendent of Police on Monday (November 23), accusing the MLA of making inappropriate advances and sending unwarranted messages. The police have booked a case against the MLA invoking provisions of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act and Sections 75, 78 and 79 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. Police sources said that Tiruppur Superintendent of Police Shristi Singh, who has been appointed as the Investigating Officer in the criminal case, began preliminary investigation into the incident on Wednesday after receiving the inquiry report from Kallakurichi Superintendent of Police I. Shahnaz at the All Women Police Station. Inspector General of Police (Administration) N. Kamini has been appointed to supervise the investigation. The National Commission for Women had earlier taken suo moto cognisance of the allegations and asked the Tamil Nadu Director General of Police to conduct an impartial inquiry. In the morning, more than 30 Democratic Youth Federation of India (DYFI) activists were arrested when they attempted to lay siege to the office of Kallakurichi TVK MLA, demanding his resignation over the allegations against him. 781240002834cf9f.title: Airtel to invest ₹1,200 cr in 3 data centers in Assam
781240002834cf9f.summary: Published - November 26, 2026 03:40 am IST - Bengaluru Image used for representational purposes only. Bharti Airtel plans to invest around ₹1,200 crore to establish three data centres in Assam, strengthening the state’s digital infrastructure and emerging as a technology investment destination. The company will invest ₹700 crore in a data centre in Guwahati, while the proposed facilities in Jorhat and Silchar will attract a combined investment of ₹500 crore. The Assam government and Bharti Airtel have signed memorandum of understanding (MoUs) for the Jorhat and Silchar projects. The two facilities will have a combined capacity of 25 MW and are expected to generate around 164 direct jobs. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said the proposed Jorhat data centre would come up on approximately four acres, with a capacity of 10 MW. The Silchar facility, spread across five acres, will have a capacity of 15 MW. Both projects will be developed in phases, with the proposed investments forming part of the company’s initial development plans. In a social media post, Mr. Sarma described the investments as a reflection of Assam’s changing economic landscape and growing investor confidence in the state. Speaking at the MoU-signing ceremony, Rajan Bharti Mittal, Vice-Chairman of Bharti Enterprises, outlined the company’s expansion plans and said land had been made available for all three proposed data centres. f2da853adbfbd977.title: Infrastructure works for Knowledge City under way, says T.N. Minister for Industries
f2da853adbfbd977.summary: Published - November 26, 2026 02:20 am IST - Chennai Tamil Nadu Minister for Industries, Investment Promotion and Commerce S. Keerthana on Tuesday said infrastructure works for Knowledge City is under way in the phase one construction of the project. She was speaking at the curtain raiser event of the India Global Education Summit 2027 (IGES) held in Chennai. The 872-acre Knowledge City is coming up in Tiruvallur district on the northern outskirts of Chennai where innovation, knowledge and research would be enhanced by bringing together universities, research labs, and research-oriented industries in a collaborative ecosystem. In the first phase, 413 acres are being developed. The Minister noted that plot allocation under this would begin by April 2027. Further, one-lakh-square-foot Knowledge Tower is also being built where plug-and-play facilities would be provided to enable foreign universities to function. Sources in Tamil Nadu Industrial Development Corporation Limited (TIDCO) noted that the tower would be ready by the later part of 2028. Speaking about the project, Ms. Keerthana said, “Institutions such as University of Melbourne and IIT Madras are already engaged with us. Further, five institutions have already signed memorandums of understanding to take up space there.” The second edition of the IGES will take place from February 3, 2027 to February 5, 2027 in Mamallapuram. The summit aims to discuss knowledge economy which includes artificial intelligence, skilling, among others. The summit will be hosted in partnership with National Indian Students and Alumni Union (NISAU), a UK body representing universities. Minister for Artificial Intelligence, Information Technology and Digital Services R. Kumar invited people, companies and institutions to invest in the AI city and Knowledge City that has been planned in the State. Electronics Corporation of Tamil Nadu Managing Director B. Vishnu Chandran, TIDCO Chairman and Managing Director D. Karthikeyan, IIT Madras

9767e4cb3cb07ed2.title: Contract employee held at airport for possessing foreign currency
9767e4cb3cb07ed2.summary: Published - November 26, 2026 01:00 am IST - CHENNAI A 23-year-old person was arrested by the security staff of the Chennai Airport for possessing huge amount of foreign currency and attempting to smuggle it to the United Arab Emirates. A senior official of the Chennai Airport police said private passenger flight bound for Dubai was preparing for departure on Wednesday morning from the Terminal 2 departure area. Passengers who had completed all necessary procedures, including customs and immigration checks, were heading to the upper deck to board the flight. Suhaib, 23, who is a contract employee for a private firm operating at the airport, was spotted standing there with a bag. This drew the attention of the security personnel on duty. The security officials enquired with Suhaib, who was not scheduled to work at the airport, of his presence, and wanted to check the bag. On inspecting the bag, they found bundles of dollar currency worth ₹19 lakh. The security officials detained Suhaib and initiated further investigations to identify the passenger to whom the bag was to be given as hawala money. The security officials have handed over Suhaib to the Chennai Airport Customs Department, who filed a case, and arrested him for possessing illegal foreign currency. No independent candidate was elected Zila Pramukh in any district. The votes for panchayat samitis and zila parishads were counted on November 20 in 37 of the State’s 41 districts. Members elected in the panchayat polls voted on Wednesday to choose their respective heads, while the results in the remaining four districts – Kota, Baran, Karauli and Sriganganagar – will be declared in December. Renu Wala of Congress defeated BJP’s Pooja Jatav by 17 votes to 14 in Bharatpur, which is Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma’s home district. a503b9fec434cd2a.title: Burglars decamp with 15 sovereigns of gold, cash from house near Jolarpet
a503b9fec434cd2a.summary: Updated - November 26, 2026 12:34 am IST - TIRUPATTUR Burglars decamped with 15 sovereigns of gold jewellery, and around ₹1.2 lakh in cash from the house of a tribal family near Jolarpet town in Tirupattur on Wednesday. Police identified the victim as R. Siva, who belongs to the Irular community. He was living with his wife and son on the outskirts of the town. Siva went to Tiruvannamalai town for Maha Deepam day as part of Karthigai Deepam festival. When he returned home around 2 a.m., Siva opened the main entrance of the house and found cupboards in the living room and the bedroom door were broken. Police said that gold ornaments and cash kept in the cupboards were missing. The rear door of the house was damaged to gain access to the house. Based on the alert, the Jolarpet police inspected the spot. Police said sniffer dogs and fingerprint experts were roped. Footage from CCTV cameras in the house and on the route were taken to identify suspects. A case was registered and special teams were formed to nab the suspects. Further probe is under way. 46b5cff4be3d6f30.title: State to expand shipbuilding industry with new investments
46b5cff4be3d6f30.summary: Published - November 26, 2026 12:36 am IST - Chennai Tamil Nadu is strengthening its shipbuilding and maritime manufacturing ecosystem with two projects involving a combined investment of ₹2,600 crore with the potential to generate 7,100 jobs. The State government has signed an MoU with Sanmar Group to set up a ₹1,950-crore ship repair and small shipbuilding facility in Thoothukudi. It also signed a deal with Chennai Radha Engineering Works, which is setting up a ₹1,500-crore greenfield project in Thoothukudi. At the second edition of the VETTRI Tamil Nadu Investment and Conversion Conclave held in Chennai, a ₹1,100-crore deal was signed with Larsen & Toubro for a project in Tiruvallur. Some of these projects will manufacture components for the shipbuilding industry. Thoothukudi is emerging as a major shipbuilding hub. A few months ago, South Korean shipbuilding major, HD Hyundai, through its shipbuilding arm, HD Korea Shipbuilding and Offshore Engineering, proposed a $4-billion greenfield mega shipyard and maritime cluster in Thoothukudi. The project is being executed, a senior government official said. The Krishnagiri district secured investment commitments of ₹9,542 crore through new MoUs, projects for which foundation stones were laid, and facilities that were inaugurated. Among the companies whose projects reached the foundation stone or inauguration stage were Ultraviolette Automotive, Uno Minda, and Sedemac Mechatronics. MoUs were also signed for 12 Multi-Modal Logistics Parks, involving an investment of ₹15,250 crore with the potential to generate jobs for 8,375 persons. According to details from the Industries Department, investments will be directed towards industrially backward districts, including Sivaganga, Dharmapuri, Virudhunagar, Cuddalore, Villupuram, Ramanathapuram, Tiruvannamalai, and Theni. 40f9e3fd97d2569d.title: Fifty years ago | 10 dead, thousands rendered homeless in floods in Madras
40f9e3fd97d2569d.summary: Published - November 26, 2026 04:40 am IST Madras, November 25: At least ten lives were lost and thousands of people rendered homeless in Madras in the floods caused by the unprecedented rain on Wednesday — 45 cm (18 inches) in 24 hours. Many of the residential areas were inundated by the overflowing Cooum and Adyar, the waterways crisscrossing the city. The floods were not so much due to the incessant rain as due to the release of surplus water from Chembarambakkam tank, one of the biggest in Chingleput district. According to the authorities, the release of water was resorted to for ensuring the safety of the bunds and the discharge would not have caused hardship to the citizens but for the high tidal wave, which was blocking the absorption of storm water by the sea. Once the tidal wave subsides, flood waters would recede. The approval was communicated to the bank on November 23 and is subject to compliance with applicable regulatory conditions. "The RBI has accorded its approval to SBI Mutual Fund for acquiring aggregate holding of up to 9.99 per cent of the paid-up share capital or voting rights in the Bank subject to the conditions specified therein," South Indian Bank said in the filing. f13eb98dea9b19bc.title: Contract awarded to ITI Ltd. for printing licences, RCs followed due tender procedures, Kerala High Court told
f13eb98dea9b19bc.summary: Updated - November 25, 2026 01:31 am IST - KOCHI The State government has informed the Kerala High Court that the contract awarded to ITI Limited, Bengaluru, for printing driving licences and registration certificates (RCs) during the tenure of Director General of Police S. Sreejith as Transport Commissioner had followed due tender procedures. Justice A. Badharudeen had sought details of the tender awarded on a plea filed by Dipin Edavana, an assistant motor vehicle inspector from Malappuram, raising allegations of corruption and fund misappropriation against Mr. Sreejith. Mr. Edavana had claimed that Mr. Sreejith awarded the printing contract after confirming an agreement with another company in March 2023. In this regard, the court had directed the State to clarify whether the contract procedures were completed properly and to specify the amounts disbursed both before and after April 2023. K.R. Jyothilal, Additional Chief Secretary (Home), said that the contract was signed at the rate of ₹60 per card plus GST for printing non-chip PVC cards. The five-year contract was signed on April 15, 2023. He also explained that the company was paid more than ₹37.70 crore for printing licences and RCs to date. Mr. Jyothilal explained that there had been an extensive legal dispute regarding the tender, which was ultimately placed before the Supreme Court. He also produced the Government Order ratifying all actions taken by then Transport Commissioner, Mr. Sreejith, as part of entering into an agreement with ITI Limited. 22aadf9ad9019d0b.title: IIFCL IPO: Govt to part sale stake, company to issue fresh shares
22aadf9ad9019d0b.summary: The government is looking to part sale its equity shareholding in IIFCL along with a fresh issue of shares by the company in the initial public offering (IPO), which is likely by the end of the current fiscal year, an official said. The Cabinet had earlier this year approved the IPO and listing of India Infrastructure Finance Company Ltd (IIFCL), and the work is on to file a draft paper with market regulator Sebi for approval. Without disclosing the quantum of stake dilution, the official said that while the government will reduce its stake by an offer for sale, IFCL will issue fresh shares to raise capital in the IPO. Set up in 2006, IIFCL is a wholly-owned government company providing long-term finances to viable infrastructure projects and is registered as a non-deposit taking non-banking finance company with the RBI. a8be22924f31c5ce.summary: Updated - November 25, 2026 01:19 am IST Indian chess grandmaster Gukesh Dommaraju makes a move during the match against Uzbek chess grandmaster Javokhir Sindarov. | Photo Credit: Reuters There was this man-against-machine match in chess in 1998. Gukesh opted for the opening game of his World chess championship match against Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva on Tuesday. The chess world had indeed been curious about the opening in the first game of the widely anticipated match between the 20-year-olds. Sindarov began by pushing the pawn in front of him by two squares, to which Gukesh replied with a similar move. Just seven moves later, the queens were off the board, and a draw would become the likeliest result later on. And it was draw. But it wasn’t a tame, dull peace treaty. There were some anxious moves along the way, and there was also a battle on the clock, which Gukesh was losing for most of the time. There were several periods when it seemed he could get into serious time trouble that could cost him dear. At one stage, he had to make his 22 moves in 24 minutes. Sindarov, at that stage, was very comfortably placed. And then, Gukesh had some six minutes for nine moves. The Chennai Grandmaster was indeed struggling. He, however, kept his calm, even as the game continued on even terms more or less. Later on, Sindarov was also forced to take more time to make his moves. c56921ce9f45e2c5.title: No basic facilities provided for mobile medical teams, says association
c56921ce9f45e2c5.summary: Published - November 25, 2026 05:30 am IST - CHENNAI No basic facilities, including drinking water, food, and restrooms, were arranged for mobile medical units deputed for Karthigai Deepam festival in Tiruvannamalai, the Service Doctors and Post Graduates Association (SDPGA) has said. In a statement, the association said that nearly 50 to 60 mobile medical teams comprising doctors, staff nurses, attenders, and drivers were deputed by the Directorate of Public Health (DPH) and Preventive Medicine to conduct medical camps in line with the Karthigai Deepam festival in Tiruvannamalai. The association’s president, P. Saminathan said that they learned from the camp sites that the teams’ minimal needs were not attended to. No drinking water was supplied, and they were told to get food from any common “Annadhanam” stalls. There was a lack of restroom facilities, especially for women doctors and staff. No proper accommodation was arranged, and some of them were asked to stay in the nearby Primary Health Centre/local colleges, the association said. “It is disheartening to see such poor management in organising camps,” it added. Citing a letter issued by the DPH, the association said that mobile medical units from various Health Unit Districts (HUD) of Cuddalore, Kancheepuram, Chengalpattu, Tiruvallur, Salem, Vellore, Villupuram, Krishnagiri, Dharmapuri, Kallakurichi, Ranipet, and Tirupattur were deputed. Five teams were deputed from each HUD. The DPH asked the District Health Officers to deploy mobile medical teams for the Karthigai Deepam festival in Tiruvannamalai for conducting special medical camps for three days starting from November 23. Citing the communication, the SDPGA said that usually these letters emphasised accommodation and food arrangements for the teams. But there was no mention of arrangements for accommodation or instructions regarding food for the teams. Hence, the arrangements were not made at the field level, it said. Published - November 25, 2026 05:30

f7067f0a23250745.title: Coast Guard in Keralam’s Kochi rescues Filipino national who suffered stroke at sea
f7067f0a23250745.summary: Updated - November 25, 2026 02:11 am IST - KOCHI A Filipino national who suffered a stroke aboard a vessel at sea was rescued by the Indian Coast Guard, according to a communication. Allan Monsanto Atiga, 52, made a full recovery and was discharged from a private hospital here. Mr. Atiga was working as a chef aboard an oil tanker sailing from Liuheng Port in China to Kochi. On November 18, while the vessel was on the high seas, he suddenly developed weakness in his left arm and leg, according to the communication. Recognising the warning signs of a possible stroke, the ship’s authorities sought emergency assistance. The Coast Guard airlifted Mr. Atiga and transported him to the hospital. An average day across quick commerce platforms in September 2026 generated about Rs 550 crore in GMV, more than any single festive day of Diwali 2025, when even Dhanteras stayed under Rs 500 crore, the data showed. Dhanteras, the day many households traditionally buy gold, silver and utensils, remained the biggest day for quick commerce, with GMV of Rs 850-900 crore against Rs 490 crore in 2025, according to Redseer. Platforms handled about 15 million orders, or around 175 orders every second, which works out to about 1,600 orders per store across roughly 9,500 dark stores. 828f080608b47d24.title: A hundred years ago | British steel for Ceylon
828f080608b47d24.summary: Published - November 25, 2026 04:20 am IST London, November 24: In the Commons, Mr. Bellairs asked Mr. Amery to suggest to the Ceylon Government to reduce duty on British iron and steel machinery and cotton piecegoods in return for the preference the British give on large quantities of Ceylon produce. Mr. Amery pointed out that preference proposals had been rejected by the Council of Ceylon in 1921 and expressed the opinion that there would be no advantage in re-opening the matter at present, but if representations were made that any British industry was adversely affected by a particular rate of duty, he would forward them to the Governor of Ceylon. He pointed out, however, that the rates were fixed by the Legislative Council on which unofficial members were in a majority. 4ee5ad4681da89a7.title: NSEL releases ₹1,950 cr in one-time settlement, ends 14-yr payment default
4ee5ad4681da89a7.summary: The National Spot Exchange Ltd (NSEL) on Monday said it has released a one-time settlement (OTS) payout of Rs 1,950 crore to eligible claimants, bringing closure to the Rs 5,600 crore payment default crisis after nearly 14 years of legal battle. The Mumbai bench of the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) had approved the settlement scheme. The full amount was deposited in a settlement account, with payouts to eligible specified creditors scheduled for November 23, 2026. The money was paid to 63 Moons Technologies, which acted as assignee of the specified creditors. On October 8, a special court in Mumbai allowed the monetisation of assets worth about Rs 3,464 crore that were attached by the Enforcement Directorate, to help fund the settlement. The scheme was first proposed by the NSEL Investors Forum, an association representing a large number of traders. NSEL, backed by 63 Moons Technologies, accepted the proposal and filed it before the tribunal as a full and final settlement.

e482d6bae9b154ec.summary: Indian Administrative Service (IAS) Sampath Kumar, a 1997-batch officer of the Assam-Meghalaya cadre, is likely to succeed Meghalaya Chief Secretary Shakil P Ahammed. Kumar has been serving in the Meghalaya government for more than 12 years. Ahammed is scheduled to retire on November 30, 2026, according to reports. He had assumed charge as the chief secretary in September 2025. IAS Sampath Kumar has emerged as the frontrunner for the post of Chief Secretary to the Government of Meghalaya. Born in May 1970, Kumar is a 1997-batch IAS officer in the Assam-Meghalaya cadre. He holds a Bachelor of Engineering degree (Electronic and Communications Engineering) from Osmania University. He also earned a Master of Public Administration from Harvard Kennedy School, according to his LinkedIn profile. Kumar is currently serving as Additional Chief Secretary in the Meghalaya government, according to the Government of Meghalaya's website. However, his LinkedIn profile says, "I am currently designated as the Principal Secretary & Development Commissioner, Government of Meghalaya, India (Depts of Health & Family Welfare; Women & Child Development; Community & Rural Development and Programme Implementation & Evaluation Dept)." He oversees several significant portfolios, including Community and Rural Development, Social Welfare, and Health and Family Welfare. "My journey encompasses diverse roles, including spearheading rural poverty reduction initiatives and founding a women's self-help group movement, which became the catalyst for a nationwide programme. Bridging the gap between Research and Policy is at the core of my innovative strategies aimed at addressing challenges to human development for transformative outcomes," his profile on LinkedIn read. e2017abf5e24f72e.title: Fifty years ago | Round-the-clock milk supply in Bombay
e2017abf5e24f72e.summary: Published - November 24, 2026 04:50 am IST Bombay, November 23: With Bombay all set for a “milk flood” the citizens will now be able to get “milk round-the-clock” and at their doorstep also. This facility will be made available from co-operative institutions and private agencies who have been invited by the Government to take delivery of milk for distribution. Agencies with sufficient refrigeration facilities will be entrusted with the task. Mr. S. A. Solankhe, Maharashtra Minister for Dairy Development, told pressmen here on Monday that availability of milk for Bombay had risen substantially with distribution itself increasing from 6.5-lakh litres a day in November last eight-lakh litres to-day. 74ceeeb6ce83d7eb.title: Japan’s Real Baby Bump Is All Relative
74ceeeb6ce83d7eb.summary: Did Japan just experience its first baby bump in a decade? For years, it has been the poster child for low fertility, with births falling every year since 2015. But in the first six months of 2026, there was an unexpected uptick: Births of Japanese nationals rose 0.4%, or 1,379 more than in the same period in 2025. Some supporters of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi were quick to claim this as more evidence that she’s restoring the country to its former glory; others noted that, since she took office only in October 2025, all these babies were conceived under her predecessor. Coming in the year of the hinoe uma, the Fire Horse of the Chinese zodiac, it seems impressive. The last such year, 1966, put a massive dent in births thanks to a bygone superstition that girls born in the year of the Fire Horse made poor wives . But it’s certainly no sea change. In fact, the blip might be over. Births in Japan are closely linked to marriages and those are down again this year after rising for the past two years in a rebound from Covid, which suppressed encounters of all kinds. The increase is also tiny next to the more than 14% jump in births next door in South Korea. However, there is a win hiding in plain sight in Japan’s data. As the earliest industrialized country to suffer falling births, Japan remains synonymous with the problem worldwide. But in recent years almost all of the developed world has followed, including several of its neighbors, where the decline has been faster and steeper. As a result, Japan is now the surprising outlier among East Asia’s richest economies. It has the highest fertility rate of the group, at 1.14. All of its peers have fallen below 1. A rate of around 2.1 is needed to hold population levels steady. For years, many assumed that Japan’s low figure was the floor. Now the obvious question is what kept the fertility rate from tumbling below one — and are there lessons for the world in what looks like, if not success, then at least a lesser degree o

71f0dc9f4e454c14.title: Proposal for extending scholarship to Sri Lankan students to pursue medical education in Tamil Nadu
71f0dc9f4e454c14.summary: Updated - November 24, 2026 02:04 am IST Sri Lankan Deputy High Commissioner in Chennai Ganesanathan Geathiswaran called on Tamil Nadu Health Minister K.G. Arunraj recently. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT The Sri Lankan Deputy High Commission (SLDHC) in Chennai is proposing to strengthen cooperation in medical education in Tamil Nadu, including the possibility of extending scholarships to Sri Lankan students. Sri Lankan Deputy High Commissioner in Chennai Ganesanathan Geathiswaran met Health Minister K.G. Arunraj in this regard recently. “During the meeting, discussion focused on further strengthening cooperation in the field of medical education, including the possibility of extending scholarships to Sri Lankan students to pursue medical studies in Tamil Nadu under a proposed 50/50 scholarship between the government of Tamil Nadu and the university concerned,” SLDHC said in a social media post. Mr. Geathiswaran meeting with the Minister last week also explored the potential for establishing student exchange programmes for medical students and postgraduate trainees, including opportunities for clinical rotations, academic exchanges and professional engagement between medical institutions in Sri Lanka and Tamil Nadu, it said. a9e4215c6f206f07.title: A hundred years ago | India’s military problem
a9e4215c6f206f07.summary: Published - November 24, 2026 04:40 am IST London, November 23: Referring to the recent tank demonstration at Camberley, a contributor to The Daily Telegraph declares that the Imperial effect of this object lesson was the most important. So long as India clings stubbornly to the belief in the effectiveness of scattered forces of the infantry so long must the War Office maintain proportionate infantry battalions at home and India’s refusal to utilise artillery tractors involves expensive training of gunners in modern methods at home which they must unlearn when faced with horsedrawn teams in India. The contributor suggests that a force invading India would find the easiest entry through Baluchistan and lays stress on the utility of tanks and armoured cars for the defence of North-west Frontier and maintaining order in cases of mob violence. He urges India to reconsider her military problem with a view to utilising modern mechanicalised forces. The Initial Public Offering (IPO) will close on November 30, while bidding for anchor investors will take place on November 25, according to the public announcement on Monday. The public issue comprises a fresh issue of equity shares aggregating up to Rs 192 crore and an Offer For Sale (OFS) of up to 88,35,382 equity shares worth Rs 168.76 crore by existing shareholders. At the upper end of the price band, the total issue size works out to Rs 360.76 crore. The company proposes to utilise the proceeds from the fresh issue towards setting up one new centralised kitchen and two new banquets, as per the RHP (Red Herring Prospectus). A portion of the proceeds will also be invested in its material subsidiary, Foodlink Global Restaurants & Catering Services ...

10461aa8358e6483.title: Residents urge PM, President to intervene over Pallikaranai wetland restrictions
10461aa8358e6483.summary: Published - November 23, 2026 01:06 am IST - Chennai Residents of Pallikaranai, Madipakkam, Velachery, Perungudi, Thoraipakkam, Sholinganallur, Karapakkam, and Perumbakkam have sought the intervention of the President and Prime Minister to safeguard their property rights, following the Madras High Court judgment dated November 18, 2026 , imposing a 1-km construction restriction around Pallikaranai Marshland. In a representation dated November 19, the Residents’ Welfare Associations of the affected areas said the restriction had caused uncertainty among thousands of families who had been living in these localities for several decades. The representation, submitted by social activist S.M. Govindarajan, representing the associations , said several families had acquired the properties through registered transactions, possessed sale deeds and patta documents, obtained building approvals, and invested their lifetime savings in their homes. They were now facing uncertainty over property rights, construction permissions, and bank loans. While expressing support for the conservation of Pallikaranai Marshland, a Ramsar site, the associations said genuine encroachments into the wetland should be distinguished from legally owned properties in established residential areas. They sought an independent scientific survey and ground-level demarcation to distinguish the marshland, drainage channels, and ecologically sensitive areas from residential properties. They also urged the authorities to examine the Tamil Nadu State Wetland Authority’s revised interim proposal to declare 36 survey numbers, covering 128.19 hectares, as a Zone of Influence, subject to scientific verification and Supreme Court directions. The representation also sought interim relief permitting essential repairs and maintenance, wherever environmentally permissible, an opportunity for affected residents to present their grievances before the Supreme Court, and a time-bound policy on properties within the restrict

The bank had initially estimated an ECL provision requirement of Rs 9,000-10,000 crore based on preliminary manual calculations. bcfecc28ef7b5575.title: West Bengal govt in talks with farmers to acquire 997 acres in Singur: CM
bcfecc28ef7b5575.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Sunday said his government was in talks with farmers to acquire 997 acres of land in Singur in Hooghly district, a day after Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar announced Ashok Leyland would set up a truck manufacturing plant there. Singur was the site of Tata Motors' Nano small-car factory, for which the then Left Front government acquired around 997 acres in 2006. The acquisition triggered a prolonged farmers' agitation led by Mamata Banerjee, following which Tata Motors moved the project to Sanand in Gujarat in 2008. In August 2016, the Supreme Court quashed the land acquisition and ordered that the land be returned to the farmers. "The West Bengal Industrial Development Corporation (WBIDC) had been tasked with acquiring the 997 acres, and negotiations with farmers were underway to purchase the land at a reasonable rate," Adhikari told reporters. He said the government would "do something" with the land, without mentioning Ashok Leyland

2989b59d8978306f.title: Oil, gas import bill up 60% in Oct as Brent surges, LPG use declines
2989b59d8978306f.summary: India's net oil and gas import bill rose 60 per cent year-on-year to USD 16 billion in October as Brent crude averaged USD 124.77 a barrel, almost double that of a year earlier, according to data from the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC), part of the oil ministry. The net bill was USD 10.0 billion in October 2025. Crude imports alone cost USD 19.5 billion, against USD 10.4 billion a year ago, even though volumes rose only 11 per cent to 23.3 million tonnes. LNG imports cost USD 1.3 billion, and petroleum product exports brought in USD 6.3 billion. Brent averaged USD 116.77 in September and USD 64.75 in October 2025. The Indian basket averaged USD 119.91 in October, against USD 65.08 a year earlier. Over April-October, the net import bill reached USD 97.7 billion, up from USD 70.3 billion a year earlier. Crude imports rose 2.7 per cent in volume but cost USD 111.0 billion, against USD 72.3 billion. Consumption of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) fell 12.3 per cent in October

6a7f60d30811e66d.title: A hundred years ago | Plea for gold currency
6a7f60d30811e66d.summary: Published - November 23, 2026 04:40 am IST Delhi, November 22: The Hon. Mr. Manmohandas Ramjee, member of the Council of State, has explained his views on the proposals for currency reform in his letter to the Bombay Government on the draft Currency Bill published by the Government of India. He is in favour of 1s. 6d. ratio, but puts forward a strong plea for the early introduction of a gold currency without which public opinion in India would not be satisfied. The 1s. 6d. ratio, he says, has been working for at least two years pretty fairly and the substitution of any other ratio at this stage would mean the unsettling of business conditions and giving firms a set-back to whatever recovery it has been possible to effect in the world of trade and industries. He does not agree with the arguement that the adjustment of prices has not taken place and that, therefore, the substitution of 1s 4d. would not lead to any unsettled conditions. He believes with the Royal Commission that adjustment of prices has taken place and that therefore, any substitution now would lead to a great deal of unfairness and injustice against particular sections of business world and also, against a large body of consumers. In an interaction with PTI, Bangur said the company is targeting a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 9-10 per cent over the next six to seven years, higher than the expected 7-8 per cent growth in the overall Indian cement industry. Shree Cement Ltd (SCL), which earlier this month announced a Rs 7,000 crore investment to set up cement plants in Andhra Pradesh as part of its expansion, expects to reach 80 MTPA capacity in the next two years, he said. In response to a question on whether Shree Cement would cross 100 MTPA, Bangur told PTI: "Yes, in the next 3-4 years." SCL is having a combined investment of nearly Rs 3,500 crore to Rs 4,000 cr

f44232bb1a76c36b.title: Walkathon stresses importance of natural childbirth
f44232bb1a76c36b.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 11:11 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Nursing college students participate in a walk to promote natural birthing during a programme organised by the Society of Midwives India (SOMI) in Vijayawada, on Sunday. | Photo Credit: G. N. Rao Ensuring that childbirth is safe, dignified and empowering for a mother is a collective responsibility, said Andhra Pradesh Transport Department Employees Association, Zone-II, president M. Rajubabu. Inaugurating a walkathon, organised in response to a call by the Society of Midwives India to promote awareness of natural childbirth, in Vijayawada on Sunday, November 22, Mr. Rajubabu emphasised the importance of maternal health, proper nutrition, regular antenatal check-ups and family support. He highlighted that emotional well-being, confidence and a supportive family environment are as important as medical care during pregnancy. He described the walkathon as more than a fitness activity, calling it a movement for maternal health, safe childbirth, women’s dignity and healthier future generations. He urged students and youth to spread awareness in every community. Government Nursing College principal S. Naga Seshamma said that the initiative aimed to promote natural childbirth, reduce medically unnecessary caesarean deliveries and highlighted the vital role of trained midwives. She stressed that caesarean sections must be respected wherever medically necessary, with delivery decisions guided by the health and safety of mother and baby. Students from the Government Nursing College, Pinnamaneni Siddhartha Nursing College and BC and SC hostels enthusiastically participated. Faculty members, association representatives and women’s organisations also attended. Addressing the fifth National Skill Convocation Ceremony at the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan here, Modi said, "Today, you must have seen that there is a lot of discussion in the media and on social media. In that discussion, everyone is saying today that Modi ji said in Parliament in 2023 that you should invest your money in bonds issued by the Government of India's PSUs. You will make a fortune. Referring to the fall in prices of gold, Modi said, "A year ago, I had urged my fellow citizens that if they don't need it, please don't buy gold for a year. And I'm happy that an ordinary person like me said it, and people bought less gold, and gold prices fell." He went on to say, "Today, I'm going to say something else.

9dec6eb2521e9bc5.title: ITC extends Braille-enabled packaging to Fiama, takes total to 16 SKUs
9dec6eb2521e9bc5.summary: Alongside an industry-wide shift toward AI-enabled personalisation and algorithmic optimisation, diversified conglomerate ITC Ltd is pursuing an analogue, inclusive approach to product innovation by incorporating raised Braille text on select personal care items from its Savlon and Fiama portfolios. The initiative makes everyday consumer products more accessible to millions of visually impaired people in India, for whom routine activities such as identifying a handwash bottle or choosing the right personal care product can pose challenges. Building on Savlon's introduction of India's first Braille-enabled FMCG packaging in 2018, ITC's Personal Care Products Business has now extended the initiative to Fiama. It now has 16 SKUs from the personal care segment under accessible packaging. Braille identifiers are currently featured on technically feasible product packs, such as Savlon Antiseptic Disinfectant Liquid, Savlon Wet Wipes and Handwash Pumps, as well as Fiama Shower Gels. ITC .

b0a53c1cd2b3b729.title: Who is Cliff Savage? 36-year-old streamer lands ₹1.13 crore job to play GTA 6 for US startup
b0a53c1cd2b3b729.summary: US-based prediction market platform Kalshi has appointed 36-year-old streamer Cliff Savage to research the virtual economy of Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6). The California resident will receive more than $100,000 for playing the highly anticipated video game, analysing its in-game economy and sharing his observations with audiences. Savage was selected from a pool of more than 33,000 applicants who applied for the unusual position. Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour announced the appointment on X, saying Savage's application “stood out the most”. Explaining why the company selected him, Mansour shared details of Savage's career journey. “He started his career as a SoundCloud artist, then discovered streaming and moved to Twitch. He hustled for a while, averaging 30 viewers per stream,” Mansour wrote. The job advertisement had offered a base salary of $100,000-$120,000 (approximately ₹ 1.13 crore) for the contract period, along with an additional $15,000 allowance for gaming and streaming expenses. The selected candidate was expected to start playing GTA 6 at midnight on its release date, November 19, and spend more than 10 hours a day exploring the game. Cliff Savage is a gaming content creator from Corona, California, who previously combined livestreaming on Twitch with occasional gig economy jobs to earn a living. Despite not having a massive online following, he managed to secure the position ahead of thousands of other applicants. A Bloomberg report said Savage had just 28 viewers watching his Twitch livestream when he received the call confirming his selection. A member of the Kalshi team, who had been keeping track of his streams, informed him about the news during the broadcast. Surprised by the announcement, Savage exclaimed, “Oh my god, bro. No way, bro,” before dropping to the floor in excitement. “I got chills in my body right now.” He later described his reaction, saying, “My whole body just went numb.” Savage also expressed his ambitions for the role in a post on X

fb560893072c2f6e.title: World chess championship: Gukesh to open title defence with black
fb560893072c2f6e.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 11:42 pm IST Javokhir Sindarov and D. Gukesh at the press conference in Geneva on Sunday. D. Gukesh will play with black pieces in the opening game of the World chess championship match against Javokhir Sindarov in Geneva. The colours were drawn at the opening ceremony on Sunday. The first game in the best-of-14 match will be played on Tuesday. Gukesh sounded confident going into the defence of his title, in spite of his inferior form. His rival, on the other hand, has had an exceptional year. “Compared to the last time, it feels like I am more experienced coming into the match, but whatever has happened till now just gets erased when we sit at the table for Game 1,” the defending champion from Chennai said. “It’s a completely different match, a completely different opponent and a different place. So I am not really thinking about other things; I just want to give my best for these 14 games.” Gukesh admitted it would be a tough test for him against Sindarov. “He has just been very consistent and in very good form,” he said. “He is surely one of the very top players who is at the very top of his game. So for sure it is going to be a real test. But I have prepared in the best way I could. I am very enthusiastic about this match, to test myself against such a strong player and to see myself what I am capable of.” Sindarov also said it would be very hard. “But I am very happy that I have got this opportunity to play for the Word championship,” he said. “There are many chess players who play all their life but do not get this chance. After winning the Candidates in Cyprus, I have been thinking about this match for the last six months, but I have been playing and a lot of travelling in that period. I will try to enjoy the match”. f7569c70ebb8177c.title: Diageo overtakes Pernod Ricard to become India's largest alco-bev firm
f7569c70ebb8177c.summary: Pernod Ricard's India revenue from operations declined 13.6 per cent in FY26 to Rs 23,701.27 crore, primarily due to the sale of its Imperial Blue business to home-grown Tilaknagar Industries, which cost the French spirits maker cede its position as India's largest alcoholic beverage player by revenue to Diageo India. Pernod Ricard India's total income, which includes other income, was at Rs 24,122.03 crore, down 12.8 per cent for the financial year ended on March 31, 2026, according to financial documents filed with the Registrar of Companies (RoC). With this, Pernod Ricard lost its crown of being the leading alco-beverage company by revenue to Diageo India (United Spirits Ltd), which is part of the British multinational alcoholic beverages company Diageo plc. Diageo India (United Spirits Ltd), part of British multinational alcoholic beverages major Diageo plc, a listed entity, had reported revenue from operations of Rs 27,816 crore and total consolidated income of Rs 28,294 crore

70f6c6c616dc4a11.title: India set to install additional 200 million air conditioners by 2035: IEA
70f6c6c616dc4a11.summary: India is set to install an additional 200 million air conditioners in homes over the next decade, making it the biggest driver of global energy demand growth, the International Energy Agency said in its World Energy Outlook 2026. The agency said India and Southeast Asia's share of the global stock of air conditioners (ACs) will rise from "less than 10 per cent today to 20 per cent by 2035". In India and Indonesia, the IEA said, "fewer than one in five households own an AC, despite high cooling needs". By comparison, around 90 per cent of households in Australia, Japan and the United States own at least one AC. The IEA said "for the first time in energy history", demand for cooling in buildings is overtaking demand for heating. India's electricity demand is likely to grow 6 per cent a year, over the next decade, under the IEA's Stated Policies Scenario, the fastest of any major region. Total energy demand is expected to rise 2.5 per cent annually, "triple the global rate". Globally

9d4e2e73cfb7706f.summary: Published - November 23, 2026 01:09 am IST - Chennai An 83-year-old person is battling for life after a stray cow knocked him down while he was riding a two-wheeler in Sembakkam near Tambaram on Saturday night. The Tambaram police said Loganathan was a resident of Pavananthiyar Street in Sembakkam near Tambaram. On Saturday night, he was riding his two-wheeler near his home to purchase grocery in the nearby street. As he was proceeding on his two-wheeler, a stray bull which was chasing a cow collided with his vehicle. In the impact, Loganathan fell from the vehicle and suffered a severe head injury. The locals rescued him and admitted him to a private hospital for treatment. The incident has gone viral on the social media. cf45f0e894ed982e.title: Kasimedu fisherfolk withdraw strike after Minister’s intervention
cf45f0e894ed982e.summary: Published - November 23, 2026 12:36 am IST - CHENNAI Fishermen of Kasimedu on Sunday withdrew their indefinite strike, seeking the release of eight boats impounded by the Andhra Pradesh government, after the intervention of Finance Minister N. Marie Wilson, who is also the MLA for Dr. Radhakrishnan Nagar Assembly constituency. The Minister, who reached the fishing harbour on Sunday morning, interacted with the leaders of various associations, and listened to their grievances for about an hour. The fisherfolk had also demanded that the State government increase the solatium paid to the kin of fishermen who died in Cyclone Murasu. Mr. Marie Wilson said he had taken up their issues with Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, and that steps would be taken to increase the compensation and bring the boats back. A former Fisheries Department official said the boats had been impounded in Andhra Pradesh since April, without the relevant provisions of the Marine Fisheries Regulation Act being implemented. “Under the Act, the Nellore Collector, should have issued notice to the boat owners, summoned them and made them pay the requisite fine. However, this has not been done.” Also, no action has been taken by the Andhra Pradesh government on the boats from Karaikal that had fished close to their coast. “The fishermen from Karaikal were the ones who had escaped along with their boats that were impounded in Andhra Pradesh,” said another source. 3498721926903552.title: WATCH | Qatari royal jet battles 65 kmph crosswinds in dramatic sideways landing in Switzerland
3498721926903552.summary: Dramatic footage of a Qatari VIP jet wrestling fierce crosswinds to land sideways at Switzerland’s Bern Airport has taken social media by storm. The 37-second clip, shared by Al Arabiya English, showed the Qatar Amiri Flight Airbus A320 visibly swaying in 65 kmph gusts before pulling off a dramatic sideways touchdown at Bern Airport. The incident reportedly occurred on Tuesday, November 17, at Belp Airport in Bern, where weather reports recorded west-south-westerly winds of 12 to 16 knots, with gusts surging up to 35 knots—roughly 65 kmph. Departing from Doha as flight QAF9, the Airbus A320-214 began its descent onto the airport’s 1,730-metre runway at around 2:40 PM local time. In the footage, the aircraft’s wings can be seen banking sharply from side to side as it descends through turbulent skies before approaching the tarmac. To counter the strong crosswinds, the pilots angled the jet’s nose into the wind—a standard aviation manoeuvre known as a “crab approach”—before straightening the aircraft moments before the landing gear touched down smoothly. According to Swiss publication 20 Minuten, aviation spotter Matthias Hänni, who filmed the descent, said he repeatedly expected the pilots to abandon the approach and climb back into the sky. Airline pilot and Swiss National Council member Thomas Hurter also told 20 Minuten that executing a go-around would have been a good option under the gusty conditions, which had reportedly forced a Swiss government aircraft to abort its own landing around the same time. As the clip—which has racked up over 4.19 lakh views on Al Arabiya English’s YouTube channel—circulated widely online, viewers speculated whether Qatar’s Emir , Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, was aboard the jet. However, Swiss media reports clarified that the Emir was not on the flight. 34e27e37c05b2507.title: Airbnb looks beyond traditional holiday hubs to deepen presence in India
34e27e37c05b2507.summary: Global hospitality platform Airbnb is looking to deepen its presence in India by expanding beyond traditional holiday destinations, strengthening the homestay ecosystem and bringing more local entrepreneurs onto its platform to tap the country's growing domestic travel market. In an interview with PTI, Airbnb India Country Manager Amanpreet Bajaj said the company's India growth strategy will focus on expanding quality accommodation supply, enabling more communities to participate in tourism and diversifying its offerings beyond stays through experiences and services. "We will also continue expanding quality supply, both in traditional leisure markets and metros and in emerging destinations such as spiritual corridors and nature-led locations. We want travellers to have more choices and local communities to benefit from tourism," Bajaj shared. He highlighted that India is one of Airbnb's fastest-growing origin markets globally, with domestic travel emerging as a major growth driver.

4d8dc7ce789bb8ae.title: Central California concert shooting: Nine people shot; one in critical condition
4d8dc7ce789bb8ae.summary: Published - November 23, 2026 04:46 am IST - Sacramento (U.S.) Image used for representational purposes only. | Photo Credit: AP Nine people were shot at a concert in central California, leaving one person critically injured with a chest injury, the local sheriff said Sunday (November 22). In pictures: America’s deadliest mass shooting The shooting broke out around 7:30 p.m. Saturday (November 21) at a concert attended by about 150 people in Strathmore, a small town in Tulare County, a mountainous region in the centre of the state, the county sheriff's department said in a statement. An unspecified number of suspects opened fire on the crowd. No arrests were announced. One 26-year-old man was shot in the chest and required surgery. He remained in critical condition, the sheriff's department said. Two other victims, ages 19 and 22, also required surgery, while six people sustained minor injuries. Authorities said that they believe the shooting “may be gang-related” but didn't elaborate. The show in the town of roughly 3,000 people featured performers from neighbouring states, the department said. The department didn't immediately respond to emailed questions seeking further details but said there was no longer any immediate threat to the public. e81f1b18443bc21d.title: EV brand E-Went eyes mass market, to test sodium-ion batteries from Dec
e81f1b18443bc21d.summary: Kolkata-based Saraogi E-Ventures, which markets electric two-wheelers under the E-Went brand, sees significant growth opportunities in India's price-sensitive markets, particularly in the sub-Rs 1 lakh segment, while exploring sodium-ion battery technology as an alternative to conventional lithium-ion batteries, its founder and CEO Umang Kumar Saraogi said. The company plans to begin trials of sodium-ion battery-powered scooters around December, deploying some vehicles for testing. The technology is being explored for its potential safety advantages over conventional lithium-ion batteries, although its relatively lower energy density makes the battery packs bulkier, Saraogi said. "It is supposed to be safer. We expect to conduct trials here starting in December and deploy some vehicles with these batteries. The economics and convenience have to be evaluated before we can deploy them in our new product launches. Currently, most of the models use lithium-ion technology," he told PTI.

The increase comes as the automaker grapples with higher price pressures despite efforts to reduce costs. The company said it would pass on part of the increased cost to the market, while seeking to limit the impact on customers. Despite sustained cost-reduction efforts, prevailing cost pressures necessitate passing on a portion of the increase to the market, while minimising the impact on customers. 79e64db5f0f9b036.title: FPIs turn aggressive buyers, invest Rs 1.18 lakh crore into Indian equities in November
79e64db5f0f9b036.summary: Foreign portfolio investors have become net buyers of Indian equities, making substantial investments in November. They have invested over ₹1.18 lakh crore so far, indicating a strong market reversal. Previously, FPIs were net sellers, offloading equities worth around ₹5.51 lakh crore from October 2024 to mid-October 2026. The recent buying trend has occurred over 13 consecutive trading sessions, averaging around ₹1,450 crore per hour.

ddce85be0556323f.title: CMC honours essay, painting, quiz competition winners in Vellore
ddce85be0556323f.summary: Published - November 23, 2026 01:00 am IST - VELLORE CMC organised essay and painting competition for VIII-XII students along with a quiz competition for school teachers. To mark World Diabetes Day 2026, the Department of Endocrinology, Diabetes and Metabolism, Christian Medical College and Hospital (CMC), Vellore, organised essay and painting competition for VIII-XII students along with a quiz competition for school teachers in Vellore. According to a press release, participants have to write an essay on “From classroom to community – Children leading the fight against diabetes”. Painting competition was “From screen time to Green time – keep diabetes away”. Quiz competition for teachers was related to general knowledge and non-communicable diseases. Around 185 students participated in various competitions at the event. Winners of the painting competition are Shavitha, Government Higher Secondary School in Poigai (Vellore), Siddharth of Shristi School (Vellore) and Ashwanth, IDA Scudder school, won first, second and third prizes respectively. In the teachers quiz competition, Savitha and Sreeja of Sunbeam CBSE School. Muthanara. and Anushya - Spark School, Savitha and Monisha of Shrishti Vidyashram School won first, second and third prizes respectively, the release said. 343b2473a205448f.title: Elderly couple found dead in Purasawalkam
343b2473a205448f.summary: Published - November 23, 2026 12:35 am IST - Chennai An elderly couple was found dead in a decomposed state in Purasawalkam on Sunday. The police said Dhanraj, 78, and his wife Chandra, 72, were residents of Saravana Perumal Koil Street in Purasawalkam and the couple had no children . Dhanraj, who once ran a small jewellery workshop, had retired due to old age and the couple was living peacefully. On Sunday morning, a conservancy worker cleaning the street noticed a foul odour emanating from the house. As the couple had not been seen over the past few days, the worker alerted Kilpauk police. The police found the bodies in a decomposed state and sent them to the Government Kilpauk Medical College Hospital for a post-mortem. The police have registered a case. e7ce13627d5ffd48.title: States can now appraise non-coal mining projects spread over 500 hectares
e7ce13627d5ffd48.summary: Non-coal mining projects spread up to 500 hectares (ha) will now be appraised for environmental clearance at the state level. This threshold was 250 hectares earlier. In a notification dated November 18, the Union Environment Ministry said that the amendment would help further decentralise the environment clearance process for such projects. It also noted that state-level bodies -- State Environment Impact Assessment Authorities (SEIAA) and State Expert Appraisal Committees (SEAC) -- already examine coal mining projects of up to 500 ha. While the SEIAA grants environmental clearances, the SEAC advises it in appraising the project. Under the Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) Notification, 2006, projects are categorised based on their size and potential impacts. Category A projects are appraised by the Centre-level Expert Appraisal Committee (EAC) and Category B projects by SEIAAs and SEACs. d6055af8036e39ce.summary: As many as 3,832 anganwadi centres across Maharashtra will be transformed into "smart anganwadis" equipped with e-learning tools, rainwater harvesting systems and modern kitchens, state Women and Child Development Minister Aditi Tatkare has said. Under the state government initiative, anganwadis operating on government land with electricity connections will undergo infrastructure upgrades and will be provided with hardware and software for e-learning, water purifiers, hand-washing basins and Swachh Bharat kits, the minister said in a statement. The initiative aims to provide children with a safe, child-friendly learning environment at anganwadi centres, which cater to children aged 0-6 years as well as pregnant women and lactating mothers, she said. The upgraded centres will also feature rainwater harvesting systems and modernised kitchens, she added.

13989f1d6169b162.title: Paper tiger: On the Green India Mission
13989f1d6169b162.summary: Updated - November 23, 2026 01:07 am IST That all was not well with the Green India Mission was clear even before its approval. After the UPA-I government announced it in 2008, the Ministry of Rural Development had objected to its financial design much before the Union Cabinet approved it in 2014. But the Environment Ministry proceeded anyway and retained largely the same arrangement when it revised the Mission in 2021. Following the Comptroller and Auditor General’s report, on November 19, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) upbraided the Ministry for the Mission’s virtual failure and for still not having issued the implementation guidelines for the revised form. The original 10-year vision was to expand forest and tree cover by 5 million hectares (mha), improve forest quality on another 5 mha, improve forest-related livelihoods for 3 million households, and sequester up to 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide a year. The outlay was ₹46,000 crore. In 2014, the Cabinet approved ₹13,000 crore for 1.4 mha each of the first two objectives by 2018, but to be supported to the tune of 81.5% by Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA), National Afforestation Programme (NAP), and MGNREGS funds. In 2021-22, the Ministry folded the NAP into the Mission and, in mid-2025, unveiled a revised version with an allocation of ₹12,190 crore to improve forest cover on 25 mha by 2030, including 24 mha through other schemes. The government had thus expanded the primary target but left the Mission responsible for only 1 mha. Together with the CAMPA, NAP, and MGNREGS funds never materialising, it is no surprise that the programmes to improve forest quality and forest cover have respectively fallen short by 91.8% and 97.5% vis-à-vis the 2014 target. The Environment Ministry had assembled a large programme around resources that it knew it could not control. 4ed7bcebc2ad79d2.title: CAQM asks Delhi, NCR states to set district-level pollution targets
4ed7bcebc2ad79d2.summary: The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) has asked Delhi and the NCR states to prepare action plans for 2027 to tackle air pollution and include district-level action measures in them. This is the first time that the CAQM has asked governments to formulate district-level action plans, which will help facilitate focused implementation and effective monitoring of pollution control measures at the grassroots. They will also help identify implementation gaps and enable timely corrective action, with clearly defined accountability, officials said. In an order dated November 20, the CAQM said, "Dealing with air pollution requires sustained and concerted efforts based on the airshed approach. For 2027, annual action plans shall also be prepared at the district level, in addition to the state and municipal corporation levels." "The Annual Action Plan-2027 shall contain clearly defined sector-wise actions with measurable targets, timelines and monitoring .

InvITs have already mobilised around Rs 88,000 crore through equity issuances during FY23-FY25, indicating growing investor appetite for infrastructure-backed investment opportunities, according to the Bharat InvITs Association. Among the proposed public offerings, Brookfield-backed Altius Telecom Infrastructure Trust has filed for a potential Rs 6,000-crore IPO as it seeks to convert from a privately placed to a publicly offered InvIT. 77e41026bea2bb0f.title: MPCB asks Adani firm to stop work on temporary labour camp in Satara
77e41026bea2bb0f.summary: The Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) has directed Adani Renewable Energy One Ltd to stop excavation and construction work for its temporary camp in Satara district for allegedly beginning these without obtaining the necessary environmental clearance and permissions. The labour camp in Satara's Patan taluka, some 300 kilometres from here, is part of the firm's 1500 MW Tarali Pumped Storage Project. In a stop-work notice dated November 20, the MPCB said the company had started excavation and development work at Gat Nos. 33 and 34 in Sawargahar village for a temporary labour camp and other storage activities without informing the board or obtaining the required permissions. The company had not secured environmental clearance for the excavation and development work from the competent authority, the MPCB added. The notice, issued under Section 33A of the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act 1974, and Section 31A of the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act .
