7c2098fd5f77e056.title: Activists rally on Vizag Beach Road against data centres, demand cancellation of permissions
7c2098fd5f77e056.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 11:24 pm IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Activists carry placards and a painting of a data centre on parched land during the rally against data centres on Beach Road in Visakhapatnam on Sunday. | Photo Credit: PAUL NICODEMUS Beach Road, crowded with Sunday evening visitors, became the setting for a campaign against the data centres coming up in and around Visakhapatnam city. Members of Green Visakha, an environmental NGO, marched from the RK Beach bus stop to the Bhagat Singh statue, raising slogans and handing out pamphlets to passers-by. G. Kantarao, treasurer of the organisation, said the government had not said how many jobs would be created, even as data centre capacity rose to over six gigawatts. He alleged that the government was serving corporate interests by allotting hills at Rushikonda and Yendada, and those belonging to the Simhachalam Devasthanam, to private firms. He demanded that all permissions given to these corporations be cancelled. “If the government does not cancel them, we will turn this into a people’s movement,” he said. The rally ended at the Bhagat Singh statue on purpose, Mr. Kantarao said. Just as Bhagat Singh had turned the course of the freedom struggle, the organisers hoped to turn the course of this agitation. Sai Teja, district president of the Students’ Federation of India, alleged that the “Stop Vizag Data Centre” social media account had been taken down three times, most recently two days before the rally. “Why is the government so afraid?” he asked. He said development should be sustainable and create jobs. Dhyuti, a research scientist and environmentalist, said the campaigners wanted clear information on health hazards, cooling methods and skilled jobs. Visakhapatnam was prone to drought and could not spare water and land for data centres, she said. Green Visakha secretary M. Chandrasekhar, environmental activists Jayashree Hatangadi and Tirupathi Rao, and Anuradha of the Human Rights Forum took part. Published

be6caf1bfca67d9e.title: India, Canada conclude sixth round of talks for proposed trade pact
be6caf1bfca67d9e.summary: India and Canada have concluded the sixth round of negotiations for a trade agreement, aimed at unlocking new opportunities in trade and investment, and diversifying supply chains, an official statement said on Saturday. The negotiations covered key areas, including trade in goods, trade in services, rules of origin, trade remedies, intellectual property and investment promotion, the commerce ministry said. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal held a meeting with Glenn Purves, Vice Minister of International Trade of Canada, and his delegation to review the progress of negotiations for the proposed Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (CEPA). The ten-day talks concluded on November 20. "Both sides reaffirmed their shared commitment to concluding an ambitious, balanced and commercially meaningful agreement that delivers tangible benefits to farmers, industries, businesses and Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in both countries," it said.

1610f8d0b3d08f0a.title: AIPC Tamil Nadu to support MSMEs through professional network
1610f8d0b3d08f0a.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 01:12 am IST - CHENNAI The All India Professionals’ Congress (AIPC) Tamil Nadu chapter should function as a professional support network for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), helping them access legal, financial and technical expertise, said its national chairman Madhu Goud Yaskhi at the organisation’s annual summit in Chennai on Saturday. Mr. Yaskhi proposed that chartered accountants, lawyers, engineers and IT professionals associated with the AIPC volunteer their time to help MSMEs with taxation, regulatory compliance, financial management and delayed payments. He said over ₹7 lakh crore owed to small enterprises across India remained stuck in delayed payments, with large companies often taking more than 120 days to clear dues despite the statutory 45-day limit. The AIPC could also take up delayed payments by State public sector undertakings with the Tamil Nadu government, he said. Lawyers could help MSMEs pursue their dues through legal notices, while chartered accountants could assist with invoice discounting and compliance. Outgoing AIPC chairman and Rajya Sabha MP Praveen Chakravarty said Congress needed to reconnect with professionals in major urban centres, where it had lost electoral ground since 2014, he said. He also urged professionals to help implement and promote the Tamil Nadu government’s policies, including the Private University Bill, startup initiatives and tourism projects, saying the Congress’s participation in the coalition government brought responsibilities beyond its share in the Cabinet. After the event, Higher Education Minister P. Viswanathan told reporters that the Private University Bill passed by the Assembly had received the Governor’s assent. The government would prepare a standard operating procedure and issue guidelines for its implementation, he said. Now, it has become parricide,” he told the audience. “For the Sangh Parivar – it includes the BJP, the RSS, all BJP cabinet ministers – the demon is Gandhi. Mr. Modi, he said, seem to think that he needs to praise Gandhi because he is a global figure, but the hardcore footsoldiers of the Sangh Parivar detest Gandhi venomously. He was in conversation with Tamil author and novelist B. Jeyamohan. Elaborating on the reasons for such attacks on Gandhi, Dr. Guha emphasised that Gandhi had come to represent the feminine in the eyes of the “macho Right”, what with his non-violent policy, inter-faith harmony, his scepticism of the State, or his scepticism of progress. “Gandhi raises almost all the important questions of human existence today. RAGHUNATHAN While early years after Independence in India saw excessive veneration of Gandhi, the recent trends have shifted to a “venomous detestation” of the man by the right-wing ecosystem led by the Sangh Parivar, historian Ramachandra Guha said here on Saturday while discussing his latest book Arguments with Gandhi. “When I was young, the ethos in India was excessive veneration of Gandhi. Now, it has become parricide,” he told the audience. “For the Sangh Parivar – it includes the BJP, the RSS, all BJP cabinet ministers – the demon is Gandhi. That should be very evident from whatever they say about Gandhi. Actually, Gandhi is their core ideological enemy, as he has once been of the Left.” Dr. Guha averred. Citing an analogy, he said that Prime Minister Modi, in his article on Gandhi in the New York Times on his 150th birth anniversary, “praised him for everything except Hindu-Muslim harmony”. Mr. Modi, he said, seem to think that he needs to praise Gandhi because he is a global figure, but the hardcore footsoldiers of the Sangh Parivar detest Gandhi venomously. He was in conversation with Tamil author and novelist B. Jeyamohan. Elaborating on the reasons for such attacks on Gandhi, Dr. Guha emphasised that Gandhi had come to represent the feminine in the eyes of the “macho Right”, what with his non-violent policy, inter-faith harmony, his scepticism of the State, or his scepticism of progress. “Gandhi raises almost all the important questions of human existence today. f178aaed7009168f.title: T.N. may see solar energy installations slowing down, say energy generators
f178aaed7009168f.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 01:12 am IST - COIMBATORE Tamil Nadu, which has 10,000 MW-11,000 MW of installed solar energy capacity, may see a slowdown in solar energy installations in 2027, according to industry representatives. The single window system for obtaining approvals is not functioning effectively, finer details based on the recently-announced Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Policy should be notified by the Tamil Nadu Electricity Regulatory Commission, and costs are escalating, say solar energy investors. “No approvals have been granted for solar energy projects for almost six months now. Only now has the government started accepting the applications. Even if they are approved now, it is difficult to commission the projects by March 2027. From April next year, it is mandatory for all new projects to have BESS, and this will push the costs up,” said one of the solar energy investors in Coimbatore. “We had a detailed discussion with the TNERC on the BESS policy. The policy says there will be waiver of wheeling charges. The wheeling charges are applicable only if a consumer buys under open access. However, the policy says solar energy generators who store energy can sell it only to the State utility. There are many such issues with the policy that need better clarity in the policy ,” says AD Thirumoorthy, State Level Renewable Energy Committee Member, Government of Tamil Nadu. The single window approval system is functioning effectively for solar energy projects that come as a part of foreign direct investments. The others require multiple approvals, starting right from the rural local body heads. These lead to delays, pushing up the costs, he added. While the BESS policy is a welcome move, the Tamil Nadu Green Energy Corporation should ensure that stored solar energy is evacuated within 24 hours, so that the generator can store freshly generated energy the next day, said L. cde4ace93eda6db5.title: PM Modi to launch development projects worth ₹34,470 cr in Bihar's Vaishali
cde4ace93eda6db5.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Bihar's Vaishali district on Saturday to launch projects worth nearly 34,470 crore, including a six-lane bridge over the Ganga river, and address a public meeting, officials said. This would be the Prime Minister's first visit to the eastern state since May, when he had attended a function marking the expansion of the cabinet headed by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, the first BJP leader to lead a government in Bihar. Elaborate security arrangements, including the suspension of vehicular movement on the national and state highways concerned for a stipulated period, have been made in Vaishali and Patna for the PM's visit, they said. The 9.76-km-long six-lane bridge, which connects Bidupur block in Vaishali to Kachchi Dargah on the outskirts of Patna, has been named 'Nitish Setu', in deference to the former Bihar chief minister, on whose watch the project was conceived and came close to completion. "The PM will visit 'Nitish Setu' in Vaishali.

939b04311350f6ba.title: Trump seeks 10% cap on credit card interest rates with Democrats' support
939b04311350f6ba.summary: President Donald Trump said Saturday that he would work with the incoming Democratic Congress to cap credit card interest rates, hoping to fulfill a promise he made on the 2024 campaign trail but couldn't deliver on because of industry pressure and a lack of interest from his fellow Republicans. "I would do it. These credit card companies have made a lot," Trump told Fox News Channel's "Saturday in America." Democrats and the Republican president have both backed capping credit card interest rates, with the standard proposal being capping rates at 10 per cent. It would substantially reduce what credit card companies can charge customers. The median credit card interest rate is roughly 22.2 per cent, according to an August survey by the New York Federal Reserve. Trump proposed capping credit card interest rates in January, as part of the White House's affordability push. abbdb2f04643f301.summary: Updated - November 22, 2026 01:12 am IST - CHENNAI Congress MP Shashi Tharoor inaugurating the Raja Ravi Varma Gallery of Oleographs and Chromo Lithographs at the C.P. Ramaswami Aiyar Foundation on Saturday. | Photo Credit: J. Johan Sathyadas Congress Member of Parliament Shashi Tharoor on Saturday inaugurated the Raja Ravi Varma Gallery of Oleographs and Chromo Lithographs at the C. P. Ramaswami Aiyar Foundation (CPRAF) to mark the institution’s 60th anniversary. He also released two books, Heritage, Education and Nature – 60 years of the C.P.Ramaswami Aiyar Foundation, and A catalogue of Ravi Varma’s Oleographs and Chomo Lithographs. Speaking during the launch, Mr. Tharoor, a long-time friend of the family, said as an MP for Thiruvananthapuram, he represented a city and a region whose history is closely connected with both Sir C.P. Ramaswamy Iyer and Raja Ravi Varma. To find their legacies brought together here in Chennai in an institution that has spent 60 years serving the wider public, is a particularly happy conjunction of history. He said the lithographs of Raja Ravi Varma, while becoming familiar objects across the country, also allowed the many who were barred from entering temples to worship the deities as well. One of the most significant reforms associated with Sir C.P.’s term as Dewan of Travancore was the temple entry proclamation, he added. He praised the work of the various schools run by the Foundation. including the Saraswathi Kendra in Chennai that was the city’s first school for children with autism, dyslexia and learning disabilities. Prakash, who received the first copies of the books, said that Sir C.P. had a magnetic personality, was a tennis player, and a polyglot who could speak several languages including, French and Latin; and he was the youngest Advocate General of Madras High court. f97096ca850df3be.title: Vasan urges political parties to fight for Cauvery water rights
f97096ca850df3be.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 01:14 am IST - CHENNAI Tamil Maanila Congress (Moopanar) president G.K. Vasan on Saturday urged the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) to direct the Karnataka government to release water due to Tamil Nadu. He also sought the cooperation of political parties in Tamil Nadu in securing the State’s rights by setting aside their differences. In a statement, Mr. Vasan expressed shock over the Supreme Court dismissing Tamil Nadu’s plea seeking the release of 11 thousand million cubic feet of Cauvery water by Karnataka. He said that, in the past, the Karnataka government had not complied with the directions of the CWMA and had acted in a step-motherly manner. Farmers in the Cauvery delta are under severe economic distress due to an acute shortage of water for irrigation. The Karnataka government should understand that the Cauvery water-sharing issue and the Mekedatu issue are not only river water disputes, but also the lifelines of the people of Tamil Nadu, Mr. Vasan added. 2635f0246638e795.title: Hero FinCorp aims to double loan disbursements over next two quarters
2635f0246638e795.summary: Hero FinCorp aims to double its loan disbursement volumes over the next two quarters, after disbursing over 4.80 lakh loans across northern India between January and September this year. Financial services company Hero FinCorp Ltd is a division of two-wheeler manufacturer Hero MotoCorp. The company's growth plans will be supported by its diversified lending portfolio, distribution network and artificial intelligence-led underwriting capabilities, according to a statement. The non-banking financial company caters to diverse financing needs through a comprehensive portfolio of retail, MSME and corporate lending solutions. "Over 4.8 lakh households and businesses across seven states have chosen us this year for a two-wheeler, a car, a personal loan, working capital or a loan against property. "We aim to double our growth in the region over the next two quarters while keeping the customer's trust at the centre of every decision we make," Hero FinCorp's spokesperson said.

The Centre has fixed the guarantee at 125 days a year for each rural job card holder under the scheme. The state sought the extra days to help farmers and rural labourers affected by deficient rainfall, Khandre said. The Rural Development and Panchayat Raj minister was speaking after visiting a desilting work site at a check dam within the Adavi Somapur Gram Panchayat limits in Gadag taluk, where he interacted with workers. "Due to drought, rural people are forced to migrate in search of work. 4d91efeef6d93a25.title: PPFAS Mutual Fund has no plans to expand its 7-scheme portfolio for now, says Neil Parikh
4d91efeef6d93a25.summary: PPFAS Mutual Fund will continue operating with its current portfolio of seven schemes while not launching new ones. CEO Neil Parikh emphasized the fund's clearly defined product architecture aimed at different investment horizons. The company focuses on value investing by identifying mispriced securities and maintaining a disciplined long-term approach. Parikh highlighted the importance of patience and underlined potential short-term underperformance due to strict valuation criteria.

59a95f409159537a.title: Vijayawada girl selected for National Roller Skating Championship
59a95f409159537a.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 11:28 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Janga Harika won two silver medals at the 38th Inter-District Roller Skating Championship, held in Kakinada recently. | Photo Credit: THE HINDU Janga Harika, a Class VII student from Vijayawada, has been selected for the National-Level Roller Skating Championships after delivering an impressive performance at the 38th Inter-District Roller Skating Championship-2026. The event, organised under the aegis of the A.P. Roller Skating Association, was held on November 14 and 15 in Kakinada. Harika, who competed in the Artistic Skating category, won a silver medal in the Inline competition, another silver in the Slow Figure competition, and third place in the Solo Style Dance competition. Hailing from Vijayawada, Janga Harika is currently studying in Class VII at St. John’s Higher Secondary School, Gannavaram. Her selection for the National-Level Championships has brought immense happiness to her family, coaches, well-wishers, and sports enthusiasts. ed4e5a9832ad1c5e.title: Chennai International Book Fair 2027 to be held from January 16 to 18
ed4e5a9832ad1c5e.summary: Updated - November 22, 2026 01:08 am IST - CHENNAI Rajmohan, Minister of School Education, unveiling the logo of Chennai International Book Festival 2027 at Anna Centenary Library in Chennai on Saturday. | Photo Credit: B. VELANKANNI RAJ Minister for School Education Rajmohan on Saturday unveiled the logo of the Chennai International Book Fair (CIBF) 2027, which is scheduled to take place from January 16 to January 18, next year, at the Chennai Trade Centre. The Minister also inaugurated the training programme for global literary agents at the Anna Centenary Library in Chennai. The upcoming CIBF will be its fifth edition, with publishers, authors, and translators from more than 110 countries expected to participate. The Publishers and Booksellers Association of Thailand (PUBAT) will participate as a special guest. At the inaugural edition of the CIBF in 2023, publishers from 23 countries participated. The number of participating countries gradually rose from 40 in 2024 to 65 in 2025 and 102 in 2026. Across these editions, 415 translation grants were awarded to 183 authors for translating 258 books into 50 languages. The training programme for global literary agents, which began on November 21, will continue until December 5. Layola Mani, Chairman of the Tamil Nadu Textbook and Educational Services Corporation, and R.V. Shajeevana, Director of Public Libraries, were present at the event. Circle’s administrative efficiency, service delivery and employment opportunities. The redistribution was carried out as part of the nationwide restructuring and rebalancing of administrative units across the Department of Posts. The Directorate had recently issued an order on the redistribution of the posts. The order has resulted in the transfer of nearly 180 posts across eight cadres from Tamil Nadu to other postal circles, including Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Punjab, Assam, Andhra Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu and Kashmir and the North-East. Sources in the department said the Tamil Nadu circle has lost only a few posts in the past decade. But this time, a large share of posts, including postal assistants, multi-tasking staff, inspectors and postmen, are being redeployed. The redistribution has come under scrutiny over the absence of an adequate assessment of the workload and establishment requirements of the Tamil Nadu Circle before the posts were diverted. Tamil Nadu postal circle handles a substantial volume of postal operations. For instance, it operates nearly 3.68 crore post office savings bank accounts across the State, which is highest number in the country, sources said. Similarly, Tamil Nadu postal circle stands second in the revenue generation with Rs.1,733 crore in 2025-26 after Maharashtra. bfb228e20ab5f123.title: DMRC transplanted trees without Forest Department’s approval, official tells HC
bfb228e20ab5f123.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 04:42 am IST The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) transplanted trees removed during the construction of an underground metro line at Ajmal Khan Park without obtaining prior approval from the Delhi government’s Forest Department, the Delhi High Court was informed. The submission was made in a status report filed by the Deputy Conservator of Forests (West Division), Department of Forest and Wildlife, in response to a petition alleging that large-scale construction work was being carried out in the area, damaging fully grown trees. The petition, on which the court had earlier issued notices to the authorities, is scheduled to be heard next on November 23 by Justice Jasmeet Singh. The petitioner, advocate Arpit Bhargava, submitted that the DMRC was carrying out extensive construction work on vacant land belonging to the Delhi Development Authority on Desh Bandhu Gupta Road in Karol Bagh, behind his residence, where several large trees stand. He said substantial quantities of iron and steel rods and other construction material were being cut and processed using mechanical equipment as part of the construction work, generating smoke, dust, fumes and particulate matter. In its status report, the Forest Department said officials of the West Division conducted a joint inspection of the project site at Ajmal Khan Park on October 7, when tree transplantation work was under way. The construction is part of the Inderlok-Indraprastha Corridor of the Delhi Mass Rapid Transit System (MRTS) Project under Phase IV. According to the report, of the 534 trees at the site, 524 were to be transplanted and 10 felled. During an inspection, it was found that around 10-15 transplanted trees were showing signs of survival and new leaf growth, and remaining trees can survive in future as transplantation is under process, the report stated. “The transplantation site had not been approved by the Forest Department before the work began,” it added. Currently, the facility has also been released in the "Sandbox environment" for API users to test and make necessary changes to their systems. 5b4808b44ac4942b.title: MHA sanctions more Central forces for Tripura municipal elections
5b4808b44ac4942b.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 11:36 pm IST - Agartala The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has sanctioned an additional 25 companies of Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) for deployment during the Urban Local Body (ULB) elections in Tripura slated for November 27. State Election Commissioner (SEC) Pradip Chakraborty said the MHA has informed the State government of its decision on Saturday. He added that with local availability of the CAPF, a total of 29 companies of the Central forces will be deployed on election duties. The deployment will remain in force even after the declaration of results on December 2. The Opposition CPI(M) and Congress have long been demanding adequate deployment of Central forces alleging that the ruling BJP is trying to turn the elections into a farce through gross irregularities and use of government machinery. They have accused the State police of failing to discharge duties neutrally. The SEC had announced a schedule to hold elections for 21 ULBs including Agartala Municipal Corporation (AMC). However, the Congress and CPI(M) said clamed their candidates were prevented from filing nomination papers for five civic bodies. The BJP secured victory in five ULBs unopposed and hence, the polls will technically occur in 16 areas instead of 21. With the election campaign picking up pace, Opposition parties have alleged that their supporters are facing obstacles and threats during the door-to-door campaign. The parties have also sought the attention of the authorities after spotting several masked youth taking part in an campaign procession of the BJP in Agartala on Saturday. They alleged the youth may have been brought in from outside the State. b1169cb24f4db674.title: Man held in Tirupattur for killing two persons
b1169cb24f4db674.summary: Updated - November 22, 2026 12:36 am IST - TIRUPATTUR A special team led by Superintendent of Police Akshay Anil Wankhere inspecting the spot. | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT A 29-year-old man was arrested by Tirupattur Taluk police on Saturday for killing two persons on the outskirts of Tirupattur town a day ago over a reportedly extra marital relationship. Police identified the arrested person as V. Sanjay Gandhi, a resident of Tiruvannamalai. The victims are E. Ranjith Kumar, 30, a resident of Tiruvannamalai, and C. Malini, 45, a resident of Tirupattur. Initial inquiry revealed that Malini married Chiranjeevi and had two children. The family was living near Tirupattur town. Malini met her school friend Sanjay Gandhi at a function a few months ago and got in touch since then. Police said Malini got acquainted with Ranjith, a cab driver, when he visited her house to meet her husband for work. Sanjay got agitated over the relationship and warned Malini of dire consequences. Police said that on Friday, when Malini and Ranjith were returning to Tirupattur in a car, Sanjay noticed them. An argument broke between them. In a fit of rage, Sanjay killed them and fled the spot. Police said a few residents noticed the duo in a pool of blood and alerted police. A special team led by Superintendent of Police Akshay Anil Wankhere inspected the spot. CCTV cameras and mobile phones were tracked. Later, the police team nabbed Sanjay in the hideout in Tirupattur. A case was registered and further probe is under way. 22870d99b63f2f45.title: Residents demand halts for more long-distance trains at Melmaruvathur
22870d99b63f2f45.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 12:56 am IST - Chennai A CPI(M) leader noted that only a few express trains were stopping at the Melmaruvathur station as the Southern Railway had removed stoppages for several trains after the COVID-19 lockdown. (FILE PHOTO) | Photo Credit: D. GOPALAKRISHNAN The residents in several villages situated around Melmaruvathur have requested the Southern Railway to provide a stoppage for several mail and express trains, including Vande Bharat and Amrit Bharat trains, at the Melmaruvathur Railway Station. G. Purushothaman, secretary of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) in Seyyur taluk, has petitioned the Southern Railway to add stoppages for mail and express trains at Melmaruvathur. He said that only a few express trains were stopping at the station, as the Southern Railway had removed stoppages for Uzhavan Express, Kamban Express, and Silambu Express after the COVID-19 lockdown As Melmaruvathur was an important spiritual town, the place has also gained commercial importance. Residents of several villages, including Seyyur, Sithamur, Lathur, and Maduranthakam, also visit Chennai for studies, work, and trade. Similarly, those travelling to the southern districts for trade and education must go to Chengalpattu or Villupuram to catch long-distance trains. The residents want long distance trains to halt at Melmaruvathur as it has become a transport hub. A senior Southern Railway official said that since the provision of additional stoppages for mail and express trains at Melmaruvathur comes under the administrative purview of Zonal Headquarters, Southern Railway headquarters would have to take a decision. Regarding the extension of suburban trains beyond Chengalpattu, the railway officer said the tracks beyond Chengalpattu railway station has not been upgraded to the prescribed standards for operation of electrical multiple unit (EMU) train services. Hence the extension of EMU train services up to Melmaruvathur was operationally not feasible

He said that only a few express trains were stopping at the station, as the Southern Railway had removed stoppages for Uzhavan Express, Kamban Express, and Silambu Express after the COVID-19 lockdown As Melmaruvathur was an important spiritual town, the place has also gained commercial importance. Residents of several villages, including Seyyur, Sithamur, Lathur, and Maduranthakam, also visit Chennai for studies, work, and trade. Similarly, those travelling to the southern districts for trade and education must go to Chengalpattu or Villupuram to catch long-distance trains. The residents want long distance trains to halt at Melmaruvathur as it has become a transport hub. A senior Southern Railway official said that since the provision of additional stoppages for mail and express trains at Melmaruvathur comes under the administrative purview of Zonal Headquarters, Southern Railway headquarters would have to take a decision. Regarding the extension of suburban trains beyond Chengalpattu, the railway officer said the tracks beyond Chengalpattu railway station has not been upgraded to the prescribed standards for operation of electrical multiple unit (EMU) train services. Hence the extension of EMU train services up to Melmaruvathur was operationally not feasible

54678118d1e8a15e.title: EPF is becoming a retirement income plan. Is it a better one?
54678118d1e8a15e.summary: The Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) board in New Delhi on Thursday (November 19) approved a voluntary Systematic Withdrawal Plan (SWP) , the Labour Ministry said. Retirees can take savings in instalments, monthly, quarterly or half-yearly, instead of one lump sum. The ministry says the plan is meant to supplement pension benefits. It is voluntary and will first be open to members above 55 with over Rs 5 lakh saved. The board also eased withdrawal rules and approved in principle investing up to 3 per cent of fresh yearly inflows in alternative investment funds (AIFs), the ministry said. Table 1: What the EPFO board changed Vivek Iyer, partner and financial services risk advisory leader at Grant Thornton Bharat, says the plan addresses “a long-standing gap in India’s retirement system”. India has focused on saving for retirement, he says, but offered little help with turning those savings into income. The advisory firm’s illustration shows how it could work. A retiree at 58 with Rs 50 lakh takes Rs 40,000 a month. If the balance keeps earning 8.25 per cent, the money lasts about 24 years, to age 82. Unlike an annuity, Iyer says, the plan lets members “keep ownership and flexibility over their corpus”. If the member dies at 68, about Rs 39.6 lakh passes to the nominee, the illustration shows. Everything hinges on interest. The ministry says the remaining money will keep generating returns. Iyer says whether it keeps earning the EPF rate “is what makes the plan attractive”. Kunal Kabra, founder of Kustodian.Life, a provident fund recovery firm, says EPF interest stops three years after retirement under current rules. On Grant Thornton’s example, that would cut the 24 years to about 13, Business Standard’s calculation shows. “If the interest still stops, then this option doesn’t make any sense,” Kabra says. It is not yet clear whether the balance under the new plan escapes that rule. The ministry has not said how instalments will be taxed . It says a corres

8d05a4e99835b13a.title: T.N. to set up Statewide online registry of voluntary donors with rare blood groups
8d05a4e99835b13a.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 01:13 am IST - CHENNAI To ensure timely availability of compatible blood for patients with rare blood groups during medical emergencies, the “Tamil Nadu Rare Blood Group Donor Registry” will be established under the Tamil Nadu State Blood Transfusion Council (TNSBTC). In an order issued recently, the State government permitted the Project Director of the TNSBTC to establish the registry. The TNSBTC will develop, maintain, and periodically update the Statewide online database of voluntary donors with rare blood groups. The order directed all licensed blood centres in Tamil Nadu to identify eligible rare blood group donors and facilitate their enrolment in the registry with due consent. The council is authorised to prescribe appropriate operational guidelines, standard procedures, and mechanisms for registration, verification, updating, utilisation and confidentiality of the registry. The Project Director had said that rare blood groups posed a significant challenge in managing patients requiring urgent blood transfusion. Timely identification and mobilisation of compatible blood donors are essential to ensure uninterrupted transfusion support in times of emergency, and it is for this that the registry had been proposed. At present, information regarding donors with rare blood groups is maintained at different blood centres and is not available through a unified State-level mechanism. This may result in delays in identifying and mobilising suitable donors during critical situations. In addition, the government also permitted the TNSBTC to establish “Blood Donor Clubs” in colleges having functional Red Ribbon Clubs (RRC) in the State. Currently, 2,379 RRCs function across the State. Each blood donor club will have a faculty coordinator and a student coordinator. 8d05a4e99835b13a.raw_facts: Published - November 22, 2026 01:13 am IST - CHENNAI To ensure timely availability of compatible blood for patients with rare blood groups during medical emergencies, the “Tamil Nadu Rare Blood Group Donor Registry” will be established under the Tamil Nadu State Blood Transfusion Council (TNSBTC). In an order issued recently, the State government permitted the Project Director of the TNSBTC to establish the registry. The TNSBTC will develop, maintain, and periodically update the Statewide online database of voluntary donors with rare blood groups. The order directed all licensed blood centres in Tamil Nadu to identify eligible rare blood group donors and facilitate their enrolment in the registry with due consent. The council is authorised to prescribe appropriate operational guidelines, standard procedures, and mechanisms for registration, verification, updating, utilisation and confidentiality of the registry. The Project Director had said that rare blood groups posed a significant challenge in managing patients requiring urgent blood transfusion. Timely identification and mobilisation of compatible blood donors are essential to ensure uninterrupted transfusion support in times of emergency, and it is for this that the registry had been proposed. At present, information regarding donors with rare blood groups is maintained at different blood centres and is not available through a unified State-level mechanism. This may result in delays in identifying and mobilising suitable donors during critical situations. In addition, the government also permitted the TNSBTC to establish “Blood Donor Clubs” in colleges having functional Red Ribbon Clubs (RRC) in the State. Currently, 2,379 RRCs function across the State. Each blood donor club will have a faculty coordinator and a student coordinator. 742391430617522f.title: 8th Pay Commission: Postal employees seek major changes in promotion rules, propose 1-4 years qualifying service
742391430617522f.summary: The Federation of National Postal Organisations (FNPO) has urged the 8th Central Pay Commission (CPC) to overhaul promotion rules for central government employees, proposing that the minimum qualifying service for promotions be fixed between one and four years, depending on the requirements of individual cadres. In a letter dated November 20 addressed to Justice Ranjana Prakash Desai, chairperson of the 8th Pay Commission, FNPO Secretary General Sivaji Vasireddy sought a comprehensive review of the existing promotion conditions specified in the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) office memorandum issued on September 20, 2022. The federation, which represents a significant section of Department of Posts employees, argued that the existing promotion framework has created prolonged career stagnation and affected the functioning of several postal offices. According to FNPO, the annexure to the DoPT memorandum prescribes widely varying qualifying service periods for promotions across different pay levels. Some promotions require employees to wait as long as 12 years. The transition from Level 6, 9 to Level 11 has the longest qualifying period of 12 years. Similarly, promotions from Level 4 to Level 6, Level 6 to Level 10 and Level 11 to Level 13 require 10 years of qualifying service. Other promotional transitions, including Level 2 to Level 4 and Level 6 to Level 9, require eight years. In contrast, several other promotions under the same framework have qualifying service requirements ranging from just one to three years, the federation pointed out. FNPO said the prolonged qualifying service requirements have adversely affected the Department of Posts, with several important positions remaining vacant for extended periods because fewer employees become eligible for promotion. The affected positions include Lower Selection Grade and Higher Selection Grade posts, supervisory positions in postal and Railway Mail Service (RMS) offices, Senior Superintendent of Post

b4d2355380c1f0e5.title: Guru Shiksha 2026 to be held in Chennai on November 27, 28
b4d2355380c1f0e5.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 01:07 am IST - Chennai The 11th edition of Guru Shiksha 2026, a State-level inter-school and inter-collegiate socio-cultural and educational programme, will be held at the Guru Nanak College and Guru Nanak Matriculation Higher Secondary School campus in Velachery on November 27 and 28, 2026. Organised by the Guru Nanak Educational Society and hosted by its Guru Nanak Centre for Consultancy and Outreach Initiatives, this year’s theme is ‘The Gurus’ Vision, A Woman’s Flight’, inspired by the vision of the Sikh Gurus. Oratorical events in English, Tamil and Hindi, poster-making, podcasts in English and Tamil, research papers in English, Tamil and Hindi, and letter-writing to Sikh Gurus in the three languages are some of the competitons. Students will be divided into five categories: Alpha (Classes I to V), Beta (Classes VI to VIII), Gamma (Classes IX to XII), Delta (college and university students and research scholars), and Epsilon (teaching and non-teaching staff and the general public, for specified competitions). The total prize limit exceeds ₹8 lakh. Online registrations are open, and spot registrations are available at the venue. acbc826c4119dbe5.summary: Published - November 22, 2026 12:50 am IST - CHENNAI The Tamil Nadu government is exploring a new site for the Hosur airport, after the site identified in Shoolagiri taluk in Krishnagiri district was rejected by the Ministry of Defence earlier this year. The new site is located near the Taneja Aerospace and Aviation Limited (TAAL) Aerodrome in Belagondapalli (about 15 km from central Hosur). Meanwhile, the Andhra Pradesh government has managed to get the site clearance for Kuppam airport project from the Ministry of Civil Aviation. This makes it even more difficult to obtain clearance for the initially identified site in Shoolagiri taluk (between Berigai and Bagalur), owing to airspace constraints. Earlier, the Tamil Nadu government had brought on board Bangalore International Airport Limited, which, over the past few weeks, had conducted a study on how to expand the site close to the TAAL airstrip and develop an airport for Hosur, sources said. The report was recently submitted to the government, based on which further discussions will be held on taking the project forward, and subsequently obtaining the site clearance. “First of all, the government had already tried twice to obtain approval for the Shoolagiri site from the Ministry of Defence, but it did not happen. The possibility for obtaining site clearance was very bleak, with Kuppam airport too vying for that airspace. As expected, Kuppam airport was granted site clearance. The Shoolagiri site was also facing stiff opposition to land acquisition from the residents. Keeping all this in mind, the site near TAAL is being considered now,” a source said. For the site near TAAL too, the State government must obtain approval from the Ministry of Defence, as the airspace is controlled by the Hindustan Aeronautics Limited. 4eca0410d663e864.title: USFDA flags 7 likely violations in check of NATCO Pharma's Hyderabad unit
4eca0410d663e864.summary: NATCO Pharma Limited on Saturday said it has received seven observations from the US health regulator following an inspection of its manufacturing facility in Kothur, Hyderabad. The US Food and Drug Administration (USFDA) conducted an inspection of the company's plant during November 12-20, NATCO Pharma said in a regulatory filing. Upon conclusion of the inspection, the company received seven observations in Form 483, it added. In USFDA parlance, a Form-483 is issued to a firm's management at the conclusion of an inspection when investigators observe conditions that, in their judgment, may constitute violations of the laws. "The company believes that the observations are procedural in nature and is confident of addressing these observations comprehensively within stipulated timelines," NATCO Pharma said.

7a1a7a181cda5ce7.title: Nikhil Gupta sentenced to over 19 years in US prison for plot to kill Khalistani separatist Pannun
7a1a7a181cda5ce7.summary: Indian national Nikhil Gupta has been sentenced to more than 19 years in prison after he admitted his role in a foiled 2023 plot to kill Khalistani separatist and US citizen Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in of New York. Gupta was sentenced to 235 months by US District Judge Victor Marrero at a hearing in Manhattan Friday. According to a statement issued from the US Department of Justice , 55-year-old Gupta, in February 2026, pleaded guilty to three criminal charges linked to a plan to kill Pannun . Justice Marrero called the plot to kill the US citizen inside the country "an attack on United States sovereignty", according to a Bloomberg report. Gupta was taken into custody in the Czech Republic in June 2023 and subsequently extradited to the US. The case forms part of what US prosecutors described as a wider conspiracy that strained relations between India and the US, as well as Canada. American authorities alleged that Gupta was associated with a network linked to the Indian government that sought to target Sikh separatists living overseas. The allegations also included the killing of Hardeep Singh Nijjar , who was shot dead by masked assailants outside a Sikh temple in western Canada in June 2023. According to prosecutors, Gupta recruited a person he believed to be a contract killer to carry out the assassination of Pannun. They alleged that he acted on instructions from Vikash Yadav, an official with India's external intelligence agency. Both Gupta and Yadav were charged with murder-for-hire, conspiracy to commit murder-for-hire and conspiracy to commit money laundering. Yadav remains outside US custody. "Today's prison sentence reflects the seriousness of Nikhil Gupta's conduct and should serve as a clear warning: the Department of Justice and its law enforcement partners will pursue and hold accountable anyone who attempts to commit violence on US soil or against US citizens," US Attorney Jamie McDonald said in a statement. 60665ffeb030b75a.summary: The overhead equipment system for power supply on the Surat-Bilimora section of the 508-km-long Mumbai-Ahmedabad Bullet Train corridor was successfully energised, the railway ministry said on Saturday. "Energisation will be carried out progressively in smaller sections, under the close supervision of technical teams to ensure safety and compliance with prescribed procedures," a railway ministry press statement said. The ministry has also issued a public safety advisory, cautioning residents, commuters, construction workers and members of the public in the vicinity of the alignment against approaching or touching overhead electrical installations or undertaking any unauthorised work near the section. Officials said that although energisation does not mean the section is ready for train operations, it is a significant achievement towards that goal. 488ecaef9940c3f2.title: Shivraj Singh Chouhan unveils India's 1st home-grown H5N1 bird flu vaccine
488ecaef9940c3f2.summary: Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan unveiled the country's first indigenously developed H5N1 vaccine to protect chickens from bird flu here on Friday. The vaccine has been developed by the ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases in Bhopal, officials from the Union Agriculture Ministry said. This is the first-of-its-kind vaccine developed in India against the H5N1 virus of Clade 2.3.2.1a of the highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI), they said. Speaking on the occasion, Chouhan said, "This vaccine is an example of India's self-reliance." HPAI, commonly known as bird flu, is a serious disease affecting chickens and other birds. Outbreaks can result in almost 100 per cent mortality among infected birds. Besides the Union Agriculture Minister, Madhya Pradesh Sports and Youth Welfare and Cooperatives Minister Vishwas Sarang and Bhopal BJP MP Alok Sharma, among others, were also present at the ceremony held here.

8854a402fa731af5.title: Inauguration of Bhavan’s Margazhi Mahotsav 2026 held
8854a402fa731af5.summary: Updated - November 21, 2026 01:09 am IST - CHENNAI Dignitaries at the inauguration of the Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan’s Margazhi Mahotsav 2026 in Mylapore on Friday. | Photo Credit: V. UMESH KUMAR Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan touches the lives of millions of people directly, N. Ravi, Chairman of Bhavan’s Chennai Kendra and Director of Kasturi and Sons Limited, said on Friday. At the inauguration of Bhavan’s Margazhi Mahotsav 2026, organised in association with South Zone Cultural Centre, Mr. Ravi said the institution has a vast national and global footprint retaining its original vision, ideals, and values. Bhavan’s activities encompass culture in its widest sense and are carried out through its kendras . “This Margazhi season, there are over 2,000 music and dance performances in the city, making it one of the largest music festivals in the world. In tune with this character of the city, the Chennai Kendra has organised this festival as its flagship event. For the next 45 days, we will be featuring over 1,000 artists in the main and supporting roles,” he added. B.K. Krishnaraj Vanavarayar, Vice-President, Bharatiya Vidya Bhavan, said, “There is something each country will be proud of. As far as India is concerned, our culture is our pride and it is rooted in spirituality. All the great acharyas, political leaders, and great men have visited the Bhavan’s various branches.” K.K. Gopalakrishnan, Director, South Zone Cultural Centre, said he was glad they were able to collaborate with an organisation of a global repute like the Bhavan. Bhavan’s Chennai Kendra Vice-Chairman Nalli Kuppuswami Chetti, Secretary M. Murali, and Director K.N. Ramaswamy were among those who spoke at the event. fca58b12f1386646.title: IJCCI to lead business delegation to Japan from Nov. 30
fca58b12f1386646.summary: Updated - November 21, 2026 01:19 am IST - CHENNAI A 16-member delegation from Osaka took part in the business networking meeting held by the Indo-Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Chennai on Friday. | Photo Credit: RAGU R. The Indo-Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry (IJCCI) organised a business networking meeting with a 16-member business delegation from Osaka, Japan, to strengthen bilateral business ties and explore opportunities for trade, investment, and industrial collaboration between India and Japan. The delegation was led by Hiromitsu Morishima, Chairperson, International Business Committee, Osaka Chamber of Commerce and Industry, and Yasushi Ninomiya, Director-General, JETRO Osaka. The companies spoke about their products and business opportunities. To strengthen bilateral economic relations, IJCCI is leading a 16-member delegation to Japan from November 30 to December 4. The delegation will visit Tokyo, Yokohama, Kochi, Fukuoka, Hiroshima, and Osaka. “We particularly look forward to strengthening our engagement with Osaka, which is one of Japan’s leading commercial and industrial centres,” said IJCCI president S. Padmanabhan. “India, with its large domestic market, growing manufacturing capabilities, and developing digital economy, offers significant opportunities for Japanese businesses,” Mr. Padmanabhan added. He further said that Indian companies can benefit from Japanese technology, management practices, and innovation. a3d95c5cf6358b76.title: Same soil, different bowls: How dals sustained Dalit kitchens through scarcity
a3d95c5cf6358b76.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 06:00 am IST Shahu Patole, author of Dalit Kitchens of Marathwada ( Anna He Apoorna Brahma. ). | Photo Credit: Special arrangement When Shahu Patole was growing up in Khamgaon village, in Osmanabad taluka in Maharashtra, in the 1960s, he remembers stories of how toor dal was difficult to come by. The food crisis in the mid-1960s, triggered by two successive droughts, had made pulses scarce and expensive. Toor dal production, for instance, fell from 1.89 million tonnes to 1.13 million tonnes between 1964 and 1967, according to government data. So, traders would sell lakh dal (grass pea; Lathyrus sativus) instead of toor , which was a long-duration crop that took more than six months to mature, or adulterate toor with the cheaper, drought-resistant legume. This was despite the Indian government prohibiting the sale of lakh dal in 1961, because the slightly bitter-tasting dal was dangerous for health. It caused lathyrism, an irreversible neurological and skeletal condition (many people suffered from paralysis of the lower limbs). The fact that such dangerous alternatives continued to be consumed in certain States, shows how essential people considered dals to be. “When meat wasn’t available, we relied on dals ,” says Patole, 63, author of Dalit Kitchens of Marathwada (2024), adding that today toor , mung , chana , masur , urad , matki , chavli , and watane are the staples. 0682d324144b9209.title: Blue-green infrastructure, heat-risk modelling considered for Chennai’s Third Master Plan
0682d324144b9209.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 01:09 am IST - Chennai Integrating greenhouse gas emissions reductions, heat adaptation and flood mitigation into statutory planning, zoning regulations and master plans was discussed at the Conference on Climate Responsive Urban Planning in Chennai on Friday. The event detailed how heat-risk modelling, hydrological vulnerability assessments, and blue-green infrastructure strategies from three years of collaboration with the Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority (CMDA) are shaping statutory policies for Chennai’s Third Master Plan (2026-2046), according to a press release. Two 60-minute technical sessions covered integrating climate actions into urban planning and localising climate action. They included discussion on bridging Climate Action Plans with day-to-day spatial planning, and a presentation on the Madhavaram Local Area Plan. Marking 10 years of Chennai’s C40 Cities membership, the conference launched the Climate Action Guide for Urban Planners in India, following the 2024 Cairo global guide. The Clean Air Zones Report, Urban Planning Accelerator signing, and Chennai’s entry into Youth Reinventing Cities for a Tiruvottiyur neighbourhood were also announced. The Jameel C40 Urban Planning Climate Labs with the CMDA and the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) convened the event. 89dd9e00ee279d71.title: Holiday Expo showcases tourism destinations from India, abroad
89dd9e00ee279d71.summary: Published - November 21, 2026 12:26 am IST - VISAKHAPATNAM The two-day Holiday Expo, featuring tourism destinations from India and abroad, began at the Gadiraju Palace Convention Center in the city on Friday. More than 75 exhibitors from over 10 States and five international destinations are taking part. Rajasthan Tourism and Delhi Tourism are the partner States. Andhra Pradesh Tourism is showcasing the State’s beaches, heritage sites, pilgrim centres and nature tourism. The stalls cover hotels, resorts, airlines, cruises and travel technology. The expo is open to the travel trade and the public. “Visakhapatnam is an important and growing travel market, and we are delighted to bring this platform to the city,” said Rohit Hangal, Director, Sphere Travelmedia and Exhibitions Pvt. Ltd. Tours and Travels Association of Andhra Pradesh president K. Vijaymohan, Hotel and Restaurant Association of Andhra Pradesh president Pavan Kartheek and officials of the Rajasthan, Delhi and Andhra Pradesh tourism departments attended the inauguration. The expo ends on Saturday. The next edition will be held in Coimbatore on January 29 and 30, 2027. 9b05f1cbd283c534.title: World Bank to assist CAG in urban governance audit for 101 Indian cities
9b05f1cbd283c534.summary: New Delhi: The World bank will assist India's Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) in examining how 101 Indian cities manage their finances, build infrastructure and deliver essential public services, as growing urban needs put pressure on municipal resources. The multilateral agency will provide technical expertise and international best practices to support the audit. The CAG is conducting a multi-year audit of urban infrastructure and services, starting with urban mobility, to provide a comprehensive assessment of municipal governance, finances and service delivery. The exercise will subsequently cover water and sanitation, housing, air quality management and liveable urban environments, with a different theme taken up each year, the comptroller and auditor general K. Sanjay Murthy said on Friday. The World Bank initiative, 'Strengthening Audit Capacity and Governance Accountability in India's Urban Sector', has been endorsed by the department of economic affairs. The exercise comes against the backdrop of growing need to strengthen municipal finances through better revenue mobilization, improved cost recovery and innovative financing mechanisms that are critical for cities to meet growing infrastructure and service delivery needs. The Union budget for 2026-27 also underscored government's focus on urban infrastructure development and the need to boost finance streams of urban local bodies, particularly for their ability to diversify revenue sources, improve financial sustainability and mobilize resources for expanding civic infrastructure. Speaking at a two-day workshop on urban infrastructure financing and municipal finance in New Delhi, Murthy said the audit of 101 cities would provide a holistic and comparable assessment of how cities are performing. He called for a sectoral approach to auditing so that multiple aspects of urban development could be assessed together.
